a11y.adjust-shape-styles.meaning: Keyboard command (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter) that moves keyboard focus into the style panel for the selected shapes (or into the image/video toolbar when one media shape is selected), so styles like colour and size can be changed without a mouse. It doesn't change any style itself; it only moves focus. Listed in the Accessibility section of the keyboard shortcuts dialog.
constraints: Row label in the shortcuts dialog next to a key combo; keep short
Imperative/verbal-noun command form

a11y.enlarge-shape.meaning: Keyboard command that scales the selected shapes up by 10%. 'Enlarge' means make bigger, not zoom the view.
constraints: Row label in the shortcuts dialog's Accessibility section; keep short
Acts on all selected shapes even though English says 'shape'

a11y.enter-leave-container.meaning: Shortcuts-dialog entry for Cmd+Shift+Up/Down, which moves keyboard selection into the children of a frame or group, or back out to the parent. 'Container' means a frame or group that holds other shapes, not a storage box. The slash means 'enter or leave'.
constraints: Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short
Display only: the item does nothing when clicked

a11y.move-shape.meaning: Shortcuts-dialog entry saying the arrow keys nudge the selected shapes on the canvas. 'Move' means change position, not relocate to another page or file.
constraints: Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short
Display only

a11y.move-shape-faster.meaning: Shortcuts-dialog entry saying Shift+arrow keys nudge the selected shapes in bigger steps. 'Faster' means a larger distance per key press.
constraints: Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short
Display only

a11y.multiple-shapes.meaning: Screen-reader announcement when the selection changes to several shapes, e.g. '3 shapes selected'. It is only ever spoken with two or more shapes, but it is still a plural so that languages can use every plural form they need.

placeholders.num: Number of selected shapes, always 2 or more

constraints: Screen reader only; never shown
Provide every plural category the target language needs

a11y.open-context-menu.meaning: Shortcuts-dialog entry for Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Enter, which opens the right-click context menu at the centre of the current selection. The ellipsis means it opens a menu.
constraints: Keep the trailing ellipsis (…)
Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short
Display only

a11y.open-keyboard-shortcuts.meaning: Shortcuts-dialog entry for Cmd+Alt+/, which opens this keyboard shortcuts dialog. Read it as 'open the keyboard shortcuts', in the Accessibility section.
constraints: Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short
Display only

a11y.pan-camera.meaning: Shortcuts-dialog entry for Space+arrow keys, which scrolls the canvas view. 'Camera' is tldraw's term for the viewport; 'pan' means slide the view sideways or up/down, not a cooking pan or a photo camera.
constraints: Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short
Display only

a11y.repeat-shape.meaning: Keyboard command (Alt+R) that makes the screen reader read the selected shape's announcement again (its text, type and position). 'Repeat' means re-announce. It does not duplicate the shape.
constraints: Trap: not 'duplicate/copy the shape'
Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short

a11y.rotate-shape-ccw.meaning: Shortcuts-dialog entry for Shift+<, which rotates the selected shapes counterclockwise (anticlockwise) by a normal step.
constraints: Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short
Display only

a11y.rotate-shape-ccw-fine.meaning: Shortcuts-dialog entry for Shift+Alt+<, which rotates the selected shapes counterclockwise by a small step. '(fine)' means fine-grained or precise, not 'okay' or 'thin'.
constraints: Trap: 'fine' = small, precise increments
Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short
Display only

a11y.rotate-shape-cw.meaning: Shortcuts-dialog entry for Shift+>, which rotates the selected shapes clockwise by a normal step.
constraints: Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short
Display only

a11y.rotate-shape-cw-fine.meaning: Shortcuts-dialog entry for Shift+Alt+>, which rotates the selected shapes clockwise by a small step. '(fine)' means fine-grained or precise.
constraints: Trap: 'fine' = small, precise increments
Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short
Display only

a11y.select-shape.meaning: Shortcuts-dialog entry for Tab, which selects the next shape on the canvas in reading order. 'Next' means the following one in order.
constraints: Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short
Display only

a11y.select-shape-direction.meaning: Shortcuts-dialog entry for Cmd+arrow keys, which selects the nearest shape in the arrow's direction (up, right, down or left).
constraints: Row label in the shortcuts dialog; keep short
Display only

a11y.shape-group.meaning: Shape type name for a group shape (several shapes grouped together), spoken by the screen reader when a group is selected, e.g. 'Group. 2 of 5'. It is a noun naming the shape, not the verb 'to group'.
constraints: Noun, not a verb
Screen reader only; followed by a full stop and the position

a11y.shape-image.meaning: Shape type name for an image shape, spoken by the screen reader when an image is selected. It may come after the image's alt text, as in '<alt text>, Image. 2 of 5'.
constraints: Noun
Screen reader only

a11y.shape-index.meaning: Screen-reader position of the selected shape among its siblings, appended to the shape announcement, e.g. 'Rectangle. 2 of 7'.

placeholders.num: 1-based position of the selected shape in reading order
placeholders.total: Total number of shapes at that level (page, frame or group)

constraints: Screen reader only
Follows the shape name and a full stop; keep it a short fragment

a11y.shape-video.meaning: Shape type name for a video shape, spoken by the screen reader when a video is selected. It may come after the video's alt text.
constraints: Noun
Screen reader only

a11y.shrink-shape.meaning: Keyboard command that scales the selected shapes down by about 10%. 'Shrink' means make smaller, not zoom out the view.
constraints: Row label in the shortcuts dialog's Accessibility section; keep short

a11y.skip-to-main-content.meaning: Skip-link button that appears only when focused with the keyboard. Activating it selects the first shape on the page, scrolls to it if needed, and moves keyboard focus to the canvas (the drawing area). The key's wording ('skip to main content') differs from the English text; translate the English text.
constraints: Button text; keep short
'Canvas' is the drawing area, not fabric

a11y.status.meaning: Accessible name (aria-label) of the hidden live region where screen-reader announcements are posted. It is a noun meaning 'status updates', not a verb or a user's presence status.
constraints: Screen reader only; single word

action.align-bottom.meaning: Command that lines up the bottom edges of two or more selected shapes. Appears in the context menu, the shortcuts dialog (Alt+S) and the command palette.
constraints: Menu item; keep short
'Bottom' is an edge or direction

action.align-center-horizontal.meaning: Command that moves two or more selected shapes horizontally so their centres line up (editor.alignShapes 'center-horizontal'). The English leaves 'centre' implicit. Used in the shortcuts dialog (Alt+H), the command palette and the menus. The context menu uses the short form.
constraints: Menu item; keep short
Must stay distinct from 'Align vertically'

action.align-center-horizontal.short.meaning: Short context-menu label for 'Align horizontally' (centre shapes along the horizontal axis). 'H' abbreviates 'horizontal'.
constraints: Very short context-menu label; an abbreviation is expected
Must stay distinct from 'Align V'

action.align-center-vertical.meaning: Command that moves two or more selected shapes vertically so their centres line up (editor.alignShapes 'center-vertical'). The English leaves 'centre' implicit. Used in the shortcuts dialog (Alt+V), the command palette and the menus. The context menu uses the short form.
constraints: Menu item; keep short
Must stay distinct from 'Align horizontally'

action.align-center-vertical.short.meaning: Short context-menu label for 'Align vertically' (centre shapes along the vertical axis). 'V' abbreviates 'vertical'.
constraints: Very short context-menu label; an abbreviation is expected
Must stay distinct from 'Align H'

action.align-left.meaning: Command that lines up the left edges of two or more selected shapes. 'Left' is a direction or edge, not 'remaining'. Appears in the context menu, the shortcuts dialog (Alt+A) and the command palette.
constraints: Menu item; keep short
Trap: 'left' is a direction, not the past tense of 'leave'

action.align-right.meaning: Command that lines up the right edges of two or more selected shapes. 'Right' is a direction or edge, not 'correct'. Appears in the context menu, the shortcuts dialog (Alt+D) and the command palette.
constraints: Menu item; keep short
Trap: 'right' is a direction, not 'correct'

action.align-top.meaning: Command in the Arrange menu/toolbar (shortcut Alt+W) that moves the selected shapes (2 or more) so their top edges line up with the topmost shape's top edge. 'Top' is the edge being aligned to, not 'to the top of the page'.
constraints: Shown next to Align left/right/bottom; keep parallel in form and short

action.back-to-content.meaning: Helper button that appears when all shapes are scrolled out of view; clicking it zooms/pans the camera back to the shapes (the selection, or everything on the page). 'Content' means the shapes on the canvas.
constraints: Floating button over the canvas; keep short

action.bring-forward.meaning: Moves the selected shapes one step up in stacking (z) order, so they sit above the next overlapping shape. Shortcut Alt+]. Not about moving them on screen.
constraints: Must stay distinct from 'Bring to front' (all the way to the top)
Pairs with 'Send backward'

action.bring-to-front.meaning: Moves the selected shapes to the very top of the stacking (z) order so they are drawn above all other shapes. Shortcut ].
constraints: Must stay distinct from 'Bring forward' (one step)
Pairs with 'Send to back'

action.convert-to-bookmark.meaning: In the Edit submenu when an embed shape (e.g. an embedded YouTube/Figma frame) is selected: replaces it with a bookmark card showing a link preview for the same URL. 'Bookmark' is the tldraw link-card shape, not a browser bookmark.

action.convert-to-embed.meaning: In the Edit submenu when a bookmark (link card) shape with an embeddable URL is selected: replaces it with a live embed of that content (e.g. a playable video). 'Embed' is the noun for the embedded-content shape.

action.copy.meaning: Clipboard Copy command (Cmd/Ctrl+C): copies the selected shapes to the clipboard. A verb on a menu item, not the noun 'a copy'.
constraints: Use the locale's standard clipboard Copy term
Keep distinct from Duplicate

action.copy-as-json.meaning: Full label (keyboard shortcuts dialog, command palette) of a debug-mode-only command that copies the selected shapes (or all shapes on the page) to the clipboard as tldraw JSON data.
constraints: Keep 'JSON' as is
Clipboard copy verb, same as action.copy

action.copy-as-json.short.meaning: Short label for the same Copy-as-JSON command, shown as an item inside the 'Copy as' submenu of the menu and context menu, so it is just the format name.
constraints: Format name; normally left untranslated

action.copy-as-png.meaning: Full label (command palette, shortcuts dialog; shortcut Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+C) for copying the selected shapes, or the whole page if nothing is selected, to the clipboard as a PNG image.
constraints: Keep 'PNG' as is
Clipboard copy verb, same as action.copy

action.copy-as-png.short.meaning: Short label for Copy as PNG, shown as an item in the 'Copy as' submenu, so it is just the image format name.
constraints: Format name; normally left untranslated

action.copy-as-svg.meaning: Full label (command palette, shortcuts dialog) for copying the selected shapes, or the whole page, to the clipboard as SVG vector markup.
constraints: Keep 'SVG' as is
Clipboard copy verb, same as action.copy

action.copy-as-svg.short.meaning: Short label for Copy as SVG, shown as an item in the 'Copy as' submenu, so it is just the format name.
constraints: Format name; normally left untranslated

action.copy-hovered-styles.meaning: Keyboard-only command (Shift+Q), listed in the keyboard shortcuts dialog: takes the styles (color, fill, size, etc.) of the shape under the pointer and makes them the styles for the next shapes you draw. 'Hovered' is the shape the mouse is over; nothing goes to the clipboard.
constraints: 'Copy' here means pick up/reuse styles, not clipboard copy

action.cut.meaning: Clipboard Cut command (Cmd/Ctrl+X): removes the selected shapes and puts them on the clipboard. Not cutting with scissors.
constraints: Use the locale's standard clipboard Cut term

action.delete.meaning: Deletes the selected shapes from the canvas (Delete/Backspace key, trash icon). Undoable.
constraints: Destructive action; use the locale's standard Delete term

action.distribute-horizontal.meaning: Full label (menus, command palette; shortcut Alt+Shift+H) for spacing 3 or more selected shapes evenly along the horizontal axis, so the gaps between them are equal.
constraints: 'Distribute' means space evenly, not hand out

action.distribute-horizontal.short.meaning: Abbreviated context-menu label for Distribute horizontally: H stands for horizontal.
constraints: Very short; abbreviation letter may follow the locale's word for horizontal
Parallel with Distribute V, Flip H, Align H

action.distribute-vertical.meaning: Full label (menus, command palette; shortcut Alt+Shift+V) for spacing 3 or more selected shapes evenly along the vertical axis, so the gaps between them are equal.
constraints: 'Distribute' means space evenly, not hand out

action.distribute-vertical.short.meaning: Abbreviated context-menu label for Distribute vertically: V stands for vertical.
constraints: Very short; abbreviation letter may follow the locale's word for vertical
Parallel with Distribute H, Flip V, Align V

action.download-original.meaning: Downloads the original uploaded file behind the selected image or video shape (the source asset, not a rendered export). Shown in menus and as the tooltip of a button on the image and video toolbars.
constraints: 'Original' is the original file, not an adjective about the download

action.duplicate.meaning: Creates a copy of the selected shapes placed next to them on the canvas (Cmd/Ctrl+D). Does not touch the clipboard.
constraints: Must stay distinct from Copy (clipboard)

action.edit-link.meaning: Edit-submenu item for selected shapes that can carry a link: opens a dialog to add, change or remove the URL attached to the shape. The ellipsis signals a dialog opens.
constraints: Keep the trailing ellipsis character

action.enhanced-a11y-mode.meaning: Command-palette/shortcuts label for switching enhanced accessibility mode on or off (a user preference that makes the UI more accessible, e.g. labels in the style panel).
constraints: 'Toggle' means switch on/off

action.enhanced-a11y-mode.menu.meaning: Checkbox-style menu item in the Accessibility submenu of the help/preferences menu. Toggles enhanced accessibility mode, which turns on extra screen-reader support and announcements in the editor. It is the short menu label; the longer command-palette label is 'Toggle enhanced accessibility mode'.
constraints: Menu item beside 'Reduce motion' and 'Enable keyboard shortcuts'; keep concise
Names a mode and is not a command to the user

action.exit-pen-mode.meaning: Helper button shown while pen mode is on (stylus-only drawing, entered automatically when a pen is detected); clicking it turns pen mode off.
constraints: 'Pen' is a stylus input mode, not the pen/draw tool

action.export-all-as-png.meaning: Full label for exporting every shape on the current page (ignoring the selection) as a downloaded PNG image file. dotcom shows it as a relabeled item in its file menu.
constraints: Keep 'PNG' as is
Export = save to a file, distinct from Copy as PNG

action.export-all-as-png.short.meaning: Short label for exporting the whole page as PNG, shown as an item in the main menu's 'Export' submenu, so it is just the format name.
constraints: Format name; normally left untranslated

action.export-all-as-svg.meaning: Full label for exporting every shape on the current page (ignoring the selection) as a downloaded SVG vector file.
constraints: Keep 'SVG' as is
Export = save to a file, distinct from Copy as SVG

action.export-all-as-svg.short.meaning: Short label for exporting the whole page as SVG, shown as an item in the main menu's 'Export' submenu, so it is just the format name.
constraints: Format name; normally left untranslated

action.export-as-png.meaning: Menu and command-palette item that exports the selected shapes (or the whole page if nothing is selected) and downloads them as a PNG image file. 'Export' means save out to a file, not send abroad. PNG is a file format; leave it as is.
constraints: Full label used where context is missing, such as the command palette and keyboard shortcuts dialog
Disabled when the page has no shapes

action.export-as-png.short.meaning: Short label for the same PNG export action, shown inside an 'Export as' submenu of the main menu and context menu, where the parent already says 'Export as'. Only the file format name.
constraints: Leave the format name PNG unchanged; it is not a word to translate
Submenu item under an 'Export as' parent

action.export-as-svg.meaning: Menu and command-palette item that exports the selected shapes (or the whole page) and downloads them as an SVG vector image file. 'Export' means save out to a file. SVG is a file format; leave it as is.
constraints: Full label used where context is missing, such as the command palette
Disabled when the page has no shapes

action.export-as-svg.short.meaning: Short label for the SVG export action, shown inside an 'Export as' submenu of the main menu and context menu. Only the file format name.
constraints: Leave the format name SVG unchanged
Submenu item under an 'Export as' parent

action.fit-frame-to-content.meaning: Context-menu and command-palette action for a selected frame: resizes the frame so it tightly encloses the shapes inside it. 'Fit' means resize to match, not 'be suitable'. 'Content' means the shapes inside the frame.
constraints: Only enabled when a single frame is selected
Context menu; keep short

action.flatten-to-image.meaning: Action (Shift+F) that replaces the selected shapes with one bitmap image that looks the same. After this they are no longer editable as separate shapes. 'Flatten' means turn into an image, not make physically flat or level.
constraints: Context menu item; keep short
Changes the shapes for good (undoable only through Undo)

action.flip-horizontal.meaning: Action that mirrors the selected shapes left-to-right (across a vertical axis). 'Flip' means mirror, not turn over or throw.
constraints: Full label for the command palette, menus and the keyboard shortcuts dialog

action.flip-horizontal.short.meaning: Compact context-menu label for mirroring the selection left-to-right. 'H' abbreviates 'horizontally'.
constraints: Context menu; must stay very short
Use the locale's natural abbreviation for horizontal, or a short word; must stay distinct from the vertical version

action.flip-vertical.meaning: Action that mirrors the selected shapes top-to-bottom (across a horizontal axis). 'Flip' means mirror.
constraints: Full label for the command palette, menus and the keyboard shortcuts dialog

action.flip-vertical.short.meaning: Compact context-menu label for mirroring the selection top-to-bottom. 'V' abbreviates 'vertically'.
constraints: Context menu; must stay very short
Must stay distinct from the horizontal version

action.frame-selection.meaning: Action that wraps the currently selected shapes in a new frame (a named container shape). 'Frame' is a verb here and 'selection' is its object: put a frame around the selected shapes. It is not a noun phrase like 'the frame of the selection', and it does not mean selecting a frame.
constraints: Also the label of the Cmd+Alt+G frame toggle shortcut
Use the same word for 'frame' as the frame tool

action.group.meaning: Action (Cmd+G) that combines the selected shapes into one group so they move and select together. A verb: 'to group'. It is not the noun 'a group'.
constraints: Context menu and toolbar; keep short
Must stay distinct from Ungroup

action.insert-embed.meaning: Menu item that opens a dialog where the user pastes a URL from a supported site (YouTube, Figma, Google Maps, etc.) to place it on the canvas as an interactive embedded shape. The ellipsis shows that a dialog follows. 'Embed' is a noun here: embedded content.
constraints: Keep the trailing ellipsis (…)

action.insert-media.meaning: Menu and toolbar item that opens the system file picker so the user can choose image or video files from their device to add to the canvas. 'Media' means images and videos. The ellipsis shows that a picker follows.
constraints: Keep the trailing ellipsis (…)

action.open-command-palette.meaning: Action that opens the command palette, a searchable popup listing every editor command. The label is the feature's name.
constraints: Use the locale's usual software term for a command palette

action.open-cursor-chat.meaning: Action (shortcut /) in multiplayer rooms that opens a short chat bubble attached to the user's own mouse cursor, which other collaborators see next to it. 'Cursor' is the mouse pointer.
constraints: Not available on touch devices
Feature name; keep short

action.open-embed-link.meaning: Context-menu action when a single embed shape is selected: opens the embedded content's original URL in a new browser tab. 'Open' is a verb, not the adjective.
constraints: Context menu; keep short

action.open-kbd-shortcuts.meaning: Action that opens the dialog listing the editor's keyboard shortcuts. 'Shortcuts' means key combinations, not shortcut links. It is the action label shown in menus and the command palette. The help menu has its own item with the same English text, 'help-menu.keyboard-shortcuts'.
constraints: Menu/command label; keep short

action.pack.meaning: Arrange action, enabled with two or more shapes selected: moves the shapes into a compact arrangement with small even gaps between them. A verb meaning arrange tightly. It has nothing to do with packaging, luggage or a bundle.
constraints: Sits next to Stack, Distribute and Align in the arrange menu; keep short

action.paste.meaning: Clipboard Paste command: inserts what was last copied or cut onto the canvas. The standard Paste of Cut/Copy/Paste. It is not glue.
constraints: Use the platform's standard clipboard term
Also labels the paste-at-cursor and paste-as-plain-text shortcut variants

action.paste-error-description.meaning: Body of an error toast shown when Paste fails because the browser refused access to the clipboard. Tells the user to grant clipboard permission (in browser settings) and try again.
constraints: Toast body; full sentences

action.paste-error-title.meaning: Title of the error toast shown when pasting from the clipboard fails. Means the paste operation did not work.
constraints: Toast title; keep short

action.print.meaning: Menu item (Cmd+P) that opens the browser's print dialog to print the selected shapes or the page. The ellipsis shows that a dialog follows.
constraints: Keep the trailing ellipsis (…)

action.redo.meaning: Standard Redo command: reapplies the last change that was undone.
constraints: Use the platform's standard Undo/Redo term
Toolbar button; keep short

action.remove-frame.meaning: Action for selected frames: deletes the frame container but keeps the shapes that were inside it on the canvas. 'Remove' here means unwrap, as opposed to deleting the contents.
constraints: Keep distinct from Delete; the contents survive

action.rename.meaning: Rename a page or frame. Shown in the page menu and also used as the title of the browser prompt asking for the new name of a page or frame.
constraints: Menu item and prompt title; keep short

action.rotate-ccw.meaning: Action that rotates the selected shapes 90 degrees counterclockwise (to the left).
constraints: Must stay distinct from Rotate clockwise

action.rotate-cw.meaning: Action that rotates the selected shapes 90 degrees clockwise (to the right).
constraints: Must stay distinct from Rotate counterclockwise

action.save-copy.meaning: 'Save a copy' of the current file as a .tldr file. Exported to SDK consumers (desktop app/extension). On tldraw.com it only labels the Cmd+S shortcut, which there just blocks the browser's save-page dialog. 'Copy' is a noun (a duplicate file), not the clipboard Copy.
constraints: Menu item; keep short

action.select-all.meaning: Standard Select all command (Cmd+A): selects every shape on the current page.
constraints: Use the platform's standard term
Disabled when the page has no shapes

action.select-none.meaning: Command that clears the current selection so no shapes are selected (deselect all). The shapes are untouched; only the selection is emptied.
constraints: Command palette entry in the selection group
Counterpart of 'Select all'; keep the pair parallel

action.select-zoom-tool.meaning: Name of the zoom tool, which the Z key switches to; the user then clicks or drags to zoom the canvas. Shown in the keyboard shortcuts dialog next to its shortcut. It names a tool (a noun), not the act of zooming in or out.
constraints: Tool name: use a noun form; keep short

action.send-backward.meaning: Moves the selected shapes one step lower in the stacking (z) order, so they sit behind the shape just beneath them. Nothing is sent anywhere; 'send' means move down in the layer order.
constraints: Also used as an icon button tooltip in the actions menu
Must stay distinct from 'Send to back' (all the way) and parallel with 'Bring forward'

action.send-to-back.meaning: Moves the selected shapes to the very bottom of the stacking (z) order, behind every other shape. 'Back' is the rear of the layer stack, not a return.
constraints: Also used as an icon button tooltip in the actions menu
Must stay distinct from 'Send backward' (one step) and parallel with 'Bring to front'

action.stack-horizontal.meaning: Arranges three or more selected shapes in a single horizontal row, side by side with an even gap between them. 'Stack' means line up next to each other, not pile on top of each other.
constraints: Menu and command palette label; the context menu uses the short form

action.stack-horizontal.short.meaning: Short context-menu form of 'Stack horizontally': lines up the selected shapes in a row. 'H' abbreviates horizontally.
constraints: Context menu; keep very short and use the locale's usual abbreviation for horizontal
Must stay parallel with 'Stack V'

action.stack-vertical.meaning: Arranges three or more selected shapes in a single vertical column, one above the next with an even gap. 'Stack' means line up, not pile on top of each other.
constraints: Menu and command palette label; the context menu uses the short form

action.stack-vertical.short.meaning: Short context-menu form of 'Stack vertically': lines up the selected shapes in a column. 'V' abbreviates vertically.
constraints: Context menu; keep very short and use the locale's usual abbreviation for vertical
Must stay parallel with 'Stack H'

action.stop-following.meaning: Button shown while your view is following another collaborator's viewport in a shared board; it stops your camera tracking theirs. 'Following' means mirroring someone's view live, not following them on social media.
constraints: Helper button on the canvas; keep short

action.stretch-horizontal.meaning: Resizes two or more selected shapes so they all span the same full width as the selection's bounds (stretched to fill horizontally).
constraints: Menu and command palette label; the context menu uses the short form

action.stretch-horizontal.short.meaning: Short context-menu form of 'Stretch horizontally': makes the selected shapes fill the selection's width. 'H' abbreviates horizontally.
constraints: Context menu; keep very short and use the locale's usual abbreviation for horizontal
Must stay parallel with 'Stretch V'

action.stretch-vertical.meaning: Resizes two or more selected shapes so they all span the same full height as the selection's bounds (stretched to fill vertically).
constraints: Menu and command palette label; the context menu uses the short form

action.stretch-vertical.short.meaning: Short context-menu form of 'Stretch vertically': makes the selected shapes fill the selection's height. 'V' abbreviates vertically.
constraints: Context menu; keep very short and use the locale's usual abbreviation for vertical
Must stay parallel with 'Stretch H'

action.toggle-auto-none.meaning: Checkbox option in the 'Input device' submenu: let the app detect automatically whether a mouse or trackpad is in use. This form is shown when the scroll-wheel behavior has no device-specific default. 'Auto' means automatic, not a car.
constraints: Sibling of 'Auto (trackpad)', 'Auto (mouse)', 'Mouse' and 'Trackpad'; keep 'Auto' identical across the three variants

action.toggle-auto-pan.meaning: Checkbox option in the 'Input device' submenu: detect the input device automatically. The parenthesis tells the user that the current default treats the scroll wheel as a trackpad (scrolling pans the canvas).
constraints: Keep 'Auto' the same as in 'Auto' and 'Auto (mouse)'; the word in parentheses should match the 'Trackpad' option's label

action.toggle-auto-size.meaning: Command for selected text shapes that have a fixed width: switches them back to automatic sizing, so the box grows and shrinks to fit its text. Despite 'Toggle', it only turns auto size on.
constraints: Context menu item, hidden when not applicable; also in the command palette

action.toggle-auto-zoom.meaning: Checkbox option in the 'Input device' submenu: detect the input device automatically. The parenthesis tells the user that the current default treats the scroll wheel as a mouse (scrolling zooms the canvas).
constraints: Keep 'Auto' the same as in 'Auto' and 'Auto (trackpad)'; the word in parentheses should match the 'Mouse' option's label

action.toggle-dark-mode.meaning: Switches the app's color scheme between dark and light. This long form appears in the keyboard shortcuts dialog and other non-menu places; menus use 'Dark mode' with a checkbox.

action.toggle-dark-mode.menu.meaning: Checkbox menu item in the preferences menu; checked when the app uses the dark color scheme. Names the setting rather than an action.
constraints: Checkbox label: a noun phrase, no verb

action.toggle-debug-mode.meaning: Turns the editor's developer debug mode on or off (shows diagnostic overlays and info). Long form for the command palette and non-menu places.

action.toggle-debug-mode.menu.meaning: Checkbox menu item, checked while developer debug mode is on. Names the setting.
constraints: Checkbox label: a noun phrase, no verb

action.toggle-dynamic-size-mode.meaning: Turns dynamic size on or off: when on, new shapes and strokes are sized relative to the current zoom level, so they look the same size on screen whatever the zoom. Long form for the command palette.

action.toggle-dynamic-size-mode.menu.meaning: Checkbox preference in the menu; checked when new shapes are scaled to the current zoom level. 'Dynamic' means it adapts to zoom.
constraints: Checkbox label: a noun phrase, no verb

action.toggle-edge-scrolling.meaning: Turns edge scrolling on or off: when on, dragging something near the edge of the screen pans the canvas automatically. Long form for the command palette.

action.toggle-edge-scrolling.menu.meaning: Checkbox preference; checked when the canvas auto-pans as you drag near the screen edge.
constraints: Checkbox label: a noun phrase, no verb

action.toggle-focus-mode.meaning: Turns focus mode on or off: hides most of the UI (toolbars, menus) to leave just the canvas. Long form for the keyboard shortcuts dialog and command palette. 'Focus' is distraction-free view, not keyboard focus or camera focus.

action.toggle-focus-mode.menu.meaning: Checkbox menu item, checked while focus mode (minimal UI, canvas only) is on. Not keyboard focus.
constraints: Checkbox label: a noun phrase, no verb

action.toggle-grid.meaning: Shows or hides the background grid on the canvas (shapes also snap to it while shown). Long form for the keyboard shortcuts dialog and command palette.

action.toggle-grid.menu.meaning: Checkbox menu item, checked while the background grid is displayed on the canvas.
constraints: Checkbox label; keep short

action.toggle-invert-zoom.meaning: Reverses which way the mouse wheel zooms (wheel up zooms out instead of in). Only enabled when the input device is set to mouse. Long form for the command palette; 'invert' means reverse the direction, not invert colors.

action.toggle-invert-zoom.menu.meaning: Checkbox menu item in the Input device submenu (help menu). When checked, the mouse scroll wheel zooms in the opposite direction. Only enabled when the input device is set to Mouse. Names the setting rather than commanding: 'Invert' qualifies the zoom direction.
constraints: Checkbox menu item; keep short
'Mouse' is the pointing device, not the animal

action.toggle-keyboard-shortcuts.meaning: Default (non-menu) label of the action that turns all keyboard shortcuts on or off for the user. Used outside menus, e.g. in shortcut listings. Not shown in the command palette because turning shortcuts off would disable the palette's own shortcut.
constraints: 'Toggle' means switch on/off, not a UI toggle widget noun

action.toggle-keyboard-shortcuts.menu.meaning: Checkbox item in the Accessibility submenu. Checked means the app responds to keyboard shortcuts; unchecking disables them (useful for screen-reader or assistive keyboard users).
constraints: Checkbox menu item; the checkmark shows the state

action.toggle-lock.meaning: Locks the selected shapes so they can't be moved or edited, or unlocks them if already locked (shortcut Shift+L). Appears in the main menu Edit section, the context menu, the command palette and the keyboard shortcuts dialog. 'Locked' is the shape state being switched, not a door/keyboard lock.
constraints: Acts on selected shapes; distinct from tool lock (action.toggle-tool-lock)

action.toggle-minimap.meaning: Command palette action that shows or hides the minimap (small overview map of the canvas in the navigation panel at the bottom corner). Checkbox state reflects whether the minimap is expanded.
constraints: 'Minimap' is the canvas overview panel

action.toggle-mouse.meaning: Option in the Input device submenu (help menu): tells the app the user navigates with a computer mouse, so the scroll wheel zooms. Mutually exclusive with Trackpad and Auto.
constraints: Computer mouse (pointing device), not the animal
Single-word menu option; keep short

action.toggle-paste-at-cursor.meaning: Default (command palette / non-menu) label of a preference: when on, pasted content is placed at the mouse pointer position instead of its original/central position.
constraints: 'Paste' is clipboard paste; 'cursor' is the mouse pointer, not a text caret

action.toggle-paste-at-cursor.menu.meaning: Checkbox item in the main menu Preferences submenu. When checked, pasted content lands at the mouse pointer position.
constraints: Names a setting, not a command to paste now
'Cursor' is the mouse pointer, not a text caret

action.toggle-reduce-motion.meaning: Command palette (accessibility group) label that turns animations on or off: when on, camera and UI animations are disabled (animation speed 0).
constraints: 'Reduce motion' is the established accessibility setting name

action.toggle-reduce-motion.menu.meaning: Checkbox item in the Accessibility submenu; when checked, animations are turned off. Use the platform's conventional name for the reduced-motion accessibility setting.
constraints: Names a setting; keep short

action.toggle-snap-mode.meaning: Command palette label of a preference: when on, shapes always snap to other shapes' edges/centers while moving or resizing, without holding a modifier key.
constraints: 'Snap' means align/magnetically attach to guides, not take a photo or break

action.toggle-snap-mode.menu.meaning: Checkbox item in the main menu Preferences submenu. When checked, shapes snap to alignment guides on every move/resize, not only when holding the modifier key.
constraints: Names a setting; 'snap' is alignment snapping

action.toggle-tool-lock.meaning: Turns tool lock on/off (shortcut Q): when on, the current drawing tool stays active after creating a shape instead of returning to the select tool. Shown as the tooltip of the lock button next to the toolbar, in the keyboard shortcuts dialog and in the command palette.
constraints: Tooltip followed by the shortcut key; keep short
Distinct from locking shapes (action.toggle-lock): this keeps a tool selected

action.toggle-tool-lock.menu.meaning: Checkbox item in the main menu Preferences submenu. When checked, the selected tool stays active after use instead of switching back to Select.
constraints: Names a setting; 'lock' means keep the tool selected, not lock shapes

action.toggle-trackpad.meaning: Option in the Input device submenu (help menu): tells the app the user navigates with a laptop touchpad, so two-finger scrolling pans the canvas. Mutually exclusive with Mouse and Auto.
constraints: Single-word menu option; use the locale's usual term for a laptop touchpad

action.toggle-transparent.meaning: Command palette (export group) label: switches whether exported/copied images (PNG/SVG) have a transparent background instead of the canvas background color.
constraints: Refers to the background of exported images, not the shapes

action.toggle-transparent.context-menu.meaning: Checkbox item in the context menu's 'Copy as' and 'Export as' submenus. When checked, the copied/exported image has a transparent background. Adjective describing the export background.
constraints: Single word in a small submenu; describes the image background (if gender agreement is needed, it agrees with 'background')

action.toggle-transparent.menu.meaning: Checkbox item in the main menu's export / copy-as submenus. When checked, exported or copied images have a transparent background. Adjective describing the export background.
constraints: Single word; describes the image background (agree with 'background' if needed)

action.toggle-wrap-mode.meaning: Command palette label of a preference: when on, a selection rectangle (brush) selects shapes only when it fully encloses (wraps around) them, rather than any shape it touches.
constraints: 'Wrap' means enclosing shapes with the selection box, not text wrapping or gift wrapping

action.toggle-wrap-mode.menu.meaning: Checkbox item in the main menu Preferences submenu. When checked, drag-selection only selects shapes completely enclosed by the selection box.
constraints: 'Wrap' means fully enclose with the selection box, not text wrapping

action.undo.meaning: Reverts the last change on the canvas (Cmd/Ctrl+Z). Appears in the main menu Edit section, the quick actions toolbar (icon button tooltip), the keyboard shortcuts dialog and the command palette.
constraints: Use the standard software term; also an icon tooltip so keep short

action.ungroup.meaning: Dissolves the selected group shape so its child shapes become independent again (opposite of Group). Shown in the actions menu, context menu and keyboard shortcuts dialog; hidden when not applicable.
constraints: Pair consistently with action.group
Also an icon-button tooltip; keep short

action.unlock-all.meaning: Unlocks every locked shape on the current page at once. Main menu Edit section and command palette; disabled when nothing is locked.
constraints: 'All' means all locked shapes on the page

action.zoom-in.meaning: Magnifies the canvas one step (Cmd/Ctrl+=). Appears in the zoom menu, main menu View section, keyboard shortcuts dialog, command palette, and as the tooltip of the + button on the minimap/navigation panel.
constraints: Also a button tooltip; keep short
Camera zoom, not resizing shapes

action.zoom-out.meaning: Zooms the canvas out one step to see more (Cmd/Ctrl+-). Appears in the zoom menu, main menu View section, keyboard shortcuts dialog, command palette, and as the tooltip of the − button on the navigation panel.
constraints: Also a button tooltip; keep short
Camera zoom, not shrinking shapes

action.zoom-quick.meaning: Entry in the keyboard shortcuts dialog's View section for Shift+Z: temporarily zooms out to an overview of the whole page, lets the user point at a spot, then zooms back in there on release. Names a navigation feature.
constraints: Shortcut list entry; keep short
'Quick' modifies 'zoom' (a fast temporary zoom), not an instruction to zoom quickly

action.zoom-to-100.meaning: Resets the canvas zoom level to 100% (actual size), Shift+0. In the zoom menu, main menu View section, actions menu on small screens, keyboard shortcuts dialog and command palette.
constraints: Keep '100%' and format the percent per locale convention

action.zoom-to-fit.meaning: Adjusts the camera so all shapes on the current page fit in view (Shift+1). In the zoom menu, main menu View section, keyboard shortcuts dialog and command palette; disabled on an empty page.
constraints: 'Fit' means fit all content on screen, not resize shapes

action.zoom-to-selection.meaning: Moves and zooms the camera so the selected shapes fill the view (Shift+2). In the zoom menu, main menu View section, keyboard shortcuts dialog and command palette; disabled with no selection.
constraints: 'Selection' is the currently selected shapes

actions-menu.title.meaning: Name of the actions menu: the tooltip/title of the '…' button opening a popover of shape actions (align, group, rotate, etc.), and the accessible label of the quick-actions toolbars. Plural noun meaning 'commands/operations', not legal or stock-market actions.
constraints: Button tooltip and screen-reader toolbar label; keep short

align-style.end.meaning: Name of a text alignment option in the style panel and command palette: align text (or a shape's label) to the end of the line, i.e. right in left-to-right text. Shown as a tooltip/aria-label like 'Align — End' on an icon button. 'End' is a position, not 'finish' or 'stop'.
constraints: Keep short; appears after a picker name in a tooltip
Pairs with Start and Middle

align-style.justify.meaning: Name of the 'justify' text alignment (text stretched to fill each line evenly). This value is a legacy alignment that migrations convert to 'start', so the current style pickers don't offer it; the label exists for completeness.
constraints: Use the standard typographic term for justified text

align-style.middle.meaning: Name of a text alignment option in the style panel and command palette: center the text (or a shape's label) horizontally. Shown as a tooltip/aria-label like 'Align — Middle' on an icon button. Means centered, not 'medium' or 'average'.
constraints: Keep short; appears after a picker name in a tooltip
Pairs with Start and End

align-style.start.meaning: Name of a text alignment option in the style panel and command palette: align text (or a shape's label) to the start of the line, i.e. left in left-to-right text. Shown as a tooltip/aria-label like 'Align — Start' on an icon button. 'Start' is a position, not the verb 'begin' or 'launch'.
constraints: Keep short; appears after a picker name in a tooltip
Pairs with Middle and End

app.loading.meaning: Accessible label (aria-label) of the loading spinner shown while the tldraw editor loads; read by screen readers, not shown as visible text. 'tldraw' is the product name.
constraints: Keep 'tldraw' lowercase and untranslated
Keep the trailing ellipsis character

arrow-kind-style.arc.meaning: Name of an arrow type in the style panel's arrow-kind picker and command palette: the arrow is drawn as a single curved arc between its ends. A geometric curve, not an architectural arch.
constraints: Keep short; one word if possible
Pairs with Elbow

arrow-kind-style.elbow.meaning: Name of an arrow type in the style panel's arrow-kind picker and command palette: the arrow is routed with right-angle bends (an elbow connector, as in diagramming tools). Not the body part; use the locale's diagramming term for an elbow/orthogonal connector if one exists.
constraints: Keep short; one word if possible
Pairs with Arc

arrowheadEnd-style.arrow.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the END (tip) of an arrow, chosen in the style panel's arrowheads picker or the command palette's 'End arrowhead' submenu: a classic open V-shaped arrowhead. Shown as a tooltip like 'Arrowheads — Arrow'.
constraints: Keep short; a noun naming a shape
Translate identically to arrowheadStart-style.arrow

arrowheadEnd-style.bar.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the END of an arrow: a short straight line drawn across the arrow's tip, perpendicular to it. Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'End arrowhead' submenu. A line/stroke, not a pub or a metal rod.
constraints: Keep short; a noun naming a shape
Must differ from Pipe
Translate identically to arrowheadStart-style.bar

arrowheadEnd-style.diamond.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the END of an arrow: a diamond (rhombus) shape at the tip. Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'End arrowhead' submenu. The geometric shape, not the gemstone.
constraints: Keep short; a noun naming a shape
Translate identically to arrowheadStart-style.diamond

arrowheadEnd-style.dot.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the END of an arrow: a filled circle (dot) at the tip. Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'End arrowhead' submenu.
constraints: Keep short; a noun naming a shape
Translate identically to arrowheadStart-style.dot

arrowheadEnd-style.inverted.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the END of an arrow: a triangle pointing backwards, against the arrow's direction (an inverted triangle). Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'End arrowhead' submenu. An adjective describing the arrowhead (the arrowhead is inverted), not an action.
constraints: Keep short
If the language inflects adjectives, agree with the word for 'arrowhead'
Translate identically to arrowheadStart-style.inverted

arrowheadEnd-style.none.meaning: Arrowhead option for the END of an arrow meaning no arrowhead: the line just ends. Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'End arrowhead' submenu.
constraints: Keep short
If 'none' inflects, agree with the word for 'arrowhead'
Translate identically to arrowheadStart-style.none

arrowheadEnd-style.pipe.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the END of an arrow called 'pipe', after the vertical-stroke character |. Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'End arrowhead' submenu. A glyph shape, not a plumbing pipe or a tobacco pipe.
constraints: Keep short
Must differ from Bar
Translate identically to arrowheadStart-style.pipe

arrowheadEnd-style.square.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the END of an arrow: a filled square at the tip. Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'End arrowhead' submenu. The geometric shape, not a town square.
constraints: Keep short; a noun naming a shape
Translate identically to arrowheadStart-style.square

arrowheadEnd-style.triangle.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the END of an arrow: a closed triangle pointing in the arrow's direction. Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'End arrowhead' submenu.
constraints: Keep short; a noun naming a shape
Translate identically to arrowheadStart-style.triangle

arrowheadStart-style.arrow.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the START (tail) of an arrow, chosen in the style panel's arrowheads picker or the command palette's 'Start arrowhead' submenu: a classic open V-shaped arrowhead. Shown as a tooltip like 'Arrowheads — Arrow'.
constraints: Keep short; a noun naming a shape
Translate identically to arrowheadEnd-style.arrow

arrowheadStart-style.bar.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the START of an arrow: a short straight line drawn across the arrow's end, perpendicular to it. Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'Start arrowhead' submenu. A line/stroke, not a pub or a metal rod.
constraints: Keep short; a noun naming a shape
Must differ from Pipe
Translate identically to arrowheadEnd-style.bar

arrowheadStart-style.diamond.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the START of an arrow: a diamond (rhombus) shape. Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'Start arrowhead' submenu. The geometric shape, not the gemstone.
constraints: Keep short; a noun naming a shape
Translate identically to arrowheadEnd-style.diamond

arrowheadStart-style.dot.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the START of an arrow: a filled circle (dot). Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'Start arrowhead' submenu.
constraints: Keep short; a noun naming a shape
Translate identically to arrowheadEnd-style.dot

arrowheadStart-style.inverted.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the START of an arrow: a triangle that points the opposite way to a normal arrowhead (an inverted triangle). Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'Start arrowhead' submenu. An adjective describing the arrowhead, not an action.
constraints: Keep short
If the language inflects adjectives, agree with the word for 'arrowhead'
Translate identically to arrowheadEnd-style.inverted

arrowheadStart-style.none.meaning: Arrowhead option for the START of an arrow meaning no arrowhead: the line just ends (this is the default for the start). Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'Start arrowhead' submenu.
constraints: Keep short
If 'none' inflects, agree with the word for 'arrowhead'
Translate identically to arrowheadEnd-style.none

arrowheadStart-style.pipe.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the START of an arrow called 'pipe', after the vertical-stroke character |. Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'Start arrowhead' submenu. A glyph shape, not a plumbing pipe or a tobacco pipe.
constraints: Keep short
Must differ from Bar
Translate identically to arrowheadEnd-style.pipe

arrowheadStart-style.square.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the START of an arrow: a filled square. Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'Start arrowhead' submenu. The geometric shape, not a town square.
constraints: Keep short; a noun naming a shape
Translate identically to arrowheadEnd-style.square

arrowheadStart-style.triangle.meaning: Name of an arrowhead style for the START of an arrow: a closed triangle. Shown in the style panel's arrowheads picker and the command palette's 'Start arrowhead' submenu.
constraints: Keep short; a noun naming a shape
Translate identically to arrowheadEnd-style.triangle

assets.files.amount-too-many.meaning: Error toast title shown when the user drops or pastes more files at once than the editor allows (editor.options.maxFilesAtOnce). None of the files is added.
constraints: Short toast title

assets.files.maximum-size.meaning: Description line of the 'File size is too big' error toast, stating the size limit for an uploaded image or video.

placeholders.size: The maximum allowed file size, already formatted with its unit (e.g. '10 MB'), from formatBytes

constraints: Keep {size} exactly; it already includes the unit

assets.files.size-too-big.meaning: Error toast title shown when an image or video the user drops, pastes or inserts exceeds the maximum asset size; the file is not added. Followed by a description giving the limit.
constraints: Short toast title

assets.files.type-not-allowed.meaning: Error toast title shown when the user drops, pastes or inserts a file whose type isn't an accepted image or video format; the file is not added.
constraints: Short toast title

assets.files.upload-failed.meaning: Error toast title shown when adding a dropped or pasted file fails: the upload to storage errored, the file couldn't be read or sanitized, or it had no MIME type. 'Upload' is a noun here (the upload failed), not a command.
constraints: Short toast title

assets.url.failed.meaning: Error toast title shown when a pasted or dropped link can't be turned into a bookmark card: fetching the page's title, image and favicon failed, the URL is invalid (e.g. blocked by an ad blocker), or creating the bookmark failed. 'Preview' is the link preview card (bookmark), not a print/document preview.
constraints: Toast title; keep short
Keep 'URL' as is unless the locale has a standard term

color-style.black.meaning: Name of the black color swatch for shapes. Shown in the style panel tooltip as '<Color> — Black' and as a value in the command palette's color picker.
constraints: Standalone color name; where adjectives inflect, use the form that agrees with the locale's word for 'color' or the bare color noun, consistently across all color-style keys

color-style.blue.meaning: Name of the blue color swatch for shapes, in the style panel and the command palette color picker.
constraints: Same grammatical form as the other color-style keys

color-style.green.meaning: Name of the green color swatch for shapes, in the style panel and the command palette color picker.
constraints: Same grammatical form as the other color-style keys

color-style.grey.meaning: Name of the grey color swatch for shapes, in the style panel and the command palette color picker.
constraints: Same grammatical form as the other color-style keys

color-style.light-blue.meaning: Name of the light blue color swatch: a pale tint of blue, distinct from the 'Blue' swatch. 'Light' means pale in shade, not lightweight or illuminated.
constraints: Must stay distinct from color-style.blue
Use the same 'light' construction for all four light-* colors

color-style.light-green.meaning: Name of the light green color swatch: a pale tint of green, distinct from 'Green'. 'Light' means pale in shade.
constraints: Must stay distinct from color-style.green
Use the same 'light' construction for all four light-* colors

color-style.light-red.meaning: Name of the light red color swatch: a pale, pinkish tint of red, distinct from 'Red'. 'Light' means pale in shade.
constraints: Must stay distinct from color-style.red
Use the same 'light' construction for all four light-* colors

color-style.light-violet.meaning: Name of the light violet color swatch: a pale tint of violet/purple, distinct from 'Violet'. 'Light' means pale in shade.
constraints: Must stay distinct from color-style.violet
Use the same 'light' construction for all four light-* colors

color-style.orange.meaning: Name of the orange color swatch for shapes (the color, not the fruit), in the style panel and the command palette color picker.
constraints: Same grammatical form as the other color-style keys

color-style.red.meaning: Name of the red color swatch for shapes, in the style panel and the command palette color picker.
constraints: Same grammatical form as the other color-style keys

color-style.violet.meaning: Name of the violet (purple) color swatch for shapes, in the style panel and the command palette color picker. The color, not the flower.
constraints: Same grammatical form as the other color-style keys

color-style.white.meaning: Name of the white color swatch for shapes, in the style panel and the command palette color picker. Also the label of the 'select white color' keyboard-shortcut action (Alt+T) that sets selected shapes to white.
constraints: Same grammatical form as the other color-style keys

color-style.yellow.meaning: Name of the yellow color swatch for shapes, in the style panel and the command palette color picker.
constraints: Same grammatical form as the other color-style keys

command-palette.arrowhead-end.meaning: Name of a style picker in the command palette that sets the arrowhead at the end (tip) of the selected arrows, e.g. none, arrow, triangle, diamond. 'End' is the position on the arrow, not a verb meaning finish.
constraints: Pair with command-palette.arrowhead-start; keep parallel
Searchable list item; keep short

command-palette.arrowhead-start.meaning: Name of a style picker in the command palette that sets the arrowhead at the start (tail) of the selected arrows. 'Start' is the position on the arrow, not a verb meaning begin.
constraints: Pair with command-palette.arrowhead-end; keep parallel
Searchable list item; keep short

command-palette.cancel.meaning: Row shown in the command palette while it is asking for text input (e.g. a new page name); choosing it (or pressing Esc) abandons the input and goes back to the list without making changes.
constraints: Use the locale's standard button form for Cancel, not a conjugated verb

command-palette.delete-page.meaning: Command palette item that deletes the current page. Disabled when it is the only page.
constraints: Command form (imperative or verbal noun)

command-palette.duplicate-page.meaning: Command palette item that makes a copy of the current page. 'Duplicate' is a verb here, not the adjective 'duplicated page'.
constraints: Command form (imperative or verbal noun)
Keep 'duplicate' distinct from 'copy' terminology

command-palette.export.meaning: Heading of the command palette section with export and copy-as commands (export as SVG/PNG, copy as SVG/PNG/JSON, transparent background, print). Also matched when searching.
constraints: Section heading; a noun form usually fits better than a verb

command-palette.go-to-page.meaning: Submenu in the command palette listing the document's other pages; picking one switches to that page.
constraints: Command form; keep short

command-palette.no-results.meaning: Message shown in the command palette when the search text matches no commands.

command-palette.page-name.meaning: Placeholder in the command palette's input while renaming the current page, prompting the user to type the new page name.
constraints: Input placeholder; noun phrase

command-palette.placeholder.meaning: Placeholder text in the command palette's search input, inviting the user to type to search commands.
constraints: Keep the trailing ellipsis
Input placeholder; use the locale's usual 'Search…' form, not a conjugated verb

command-palette.recent.meaning: Heading of the command palette section listing recently run commands, shown when the search box is empty.
constraints: Refers to recent commands; adjective may need to agree with the locale's word for commands/items

command-palette.rename-page.meaning: Command palette item that asks for a new name and renames the current page.
constraints: Command form (imperative or verbal noun)

command-palette.selection.meaning: Heading of the command palette section with commands on the selected shapes (delete, duplicate, group, lock…), shown while shapes are selected. Refers to the currently selected shapes, not the act of choosing.

command-palette.title.meaning: Accessible name of the command palette dialog and its list (read by screen readers): the searchable list of all commands.
constraints: Use the locale's established term for a 'command palette' if one exists

command-palette.tools.meaning: Heading of the command palette section listing drawing tools (select, draw, rectangle, arrow, text…) to switch to.

comments.add-placeholder.meaning: Placeholder in the text box for writing a new comment pinned on the canvas, before it is sent.
constraints: Keep the trailing ellipsis
Input placeholder; invites typing a comment

comments.add-reaction.meaning: Tooltip and accessible title of the smiley-face icon button on a comment that opens the emoji reaction picker. 'Reaction' means an emoji response to a comment, not a chemical or emotional reaction.
constraints: Icon-button tooltip; keep short

comments.close.meaning: Menu item that closes a comments panel: in the comments sidebar's filter menu it closes the sidebar; in an open thread's more-options menu it closes the thread popover. Closes the view only; nothing is resolved or deleted. 'Close' is a verb, not the adjective 'near'.
constraints: Menu item; keep short

comments.cluster-label.meaning: Screen-reader label for a badge on the canvas that groups several nearby comment threads when zoomed out; pressing it zooms in or opens them. Says how many comments are grouped at that spot.

placeholders.count: Number of comment threads in the cluster, 2 or more in practice

constraints: aria-label only, not visible

comments.copy-link.meaning: Menu item in a comment thread's more-options menu that copies a URL to this thread to the clipboard. 'Copy' is the verb, not the noun 'a copy'; 'link' is a web URL. After clicking, the item changes to 'Link copied'.
constraints: Menu item; keep short

comments.delete.meaning: Menu item in a comment thread's more-options menu that permanently deletes the whole thread (the opening comment and all replies). The English says 'thread'; a single comment is deleted with a separate 'Delete' item.
constraints: Destructive action
Menu item; keep short

comments.edit.meaning: Menu item in a single comment's more-options menu that switches that comment into an editor so its author can change the text. Verb.
constraints: Menu item; keep short

comments.edit-placeholder.meaning: Placeholder text shown in the text box while the user is editing one of their existing comments. 'Edit' is an imperative verb inviting the user to change the comment.
constraints: Input placeholder; keep the trailing ellipsis character

comments.empty.meaning: Empty-state message in the comments sidebar when the current page has no comment threads at all. 'Page' is a page of the tldraw document, not a web page.

comments.empty-filtered.meaning: Empty-state message in the comments sidebar when comments exist but none pass the active filters (e.g. only mine, only unread).

comments.filter.meaning: Tooltip and title of the icon button in the comments sidebar header that opens the filter menu (show all pages, only my comments, only unread, show resolved). 'Filter' is a verb.
constraints: Icon-button tooltip; keep short

comments.hide.meaning: Toggle action that hides all comment pins from the canvas (the comments still exist). Paired with 'Show comments' when they are hidden. Appears in the comments overflow menu (with a keyboard shortcut) and as a visibility toggle button.
constraints: Menu item / toggle; keep short

comments.link-copied.meaning: Confirmation that replaces the 'Copy link' menu item's text in place after the thread's URL has been copied to the clipboard. Past participle: the link has been copied.
constraints: Shown in the same menu slot as 'Copy link'; keep similar length

comments.mention-no-matches.meaning: Shown in the @-mention suggestion dropdown in the comment composer when no person matches what the user has typed after @.
constraints: Small dropdown; keep short

comments.mention-you.meaning: Word for the current user. Shown in parentheses after the user's own name in the @-mention list, and substituted for the user's name in the reaction tooltip sentence ('You reacted', 'You and Bo reacted').
constraints: Used as a subject inside comments.reacted, so it must work as the subject of a sentence and in a list of names

comments.more-options.meaning: Tooltip, title and icon label of a three-dots button that opens a menu of extra actions: on the comments sidebar (show/hide comments) and on a thread or comment (copy link, edit, delete, close).
constraints: Icon-button tooltip; keep short

comments.only-my-comments.meaning: Checkbox item in the comments sidebar filter menu; when checked, the list shows only threads the current user started.
constraints: Checkbox menu item; keep short

comments.only-unread.meaning: Checkbox item in the comments sidebar filter menu; when checked, the list shows only threads with comments the current user hasn't read. Refers to comments/threads, not messages in general.
constraints: Checkbox menu item; keep short

comments.pin-label.meaning: Accessible label for a comment pin on the canvas, and for a thread entry in a stacked-pins list, naming who started the thread. 'Comment' is a noun here.

placeholders.name: Display name of the thread's author, or 'Someone' if unknown

constraints: aria-label only, not visible

comments.pin-label-resolved.meaning: Accessible label for a comment pin or stacked-thread entry whose thread has been resolved (marked done), naming who started it. 'Resolved' describes the comment, and the name is the comment's author, not who resolved it.

placeholders.name: Display name of the thread's author, or 'Someone' if unknown

constraints: aria-label only, not visible

comments.preview-more.meaning: Line at the bottom of the hover preview of a group of comment threads, saying how many more threads exist beyond the ones shown.

placeholders.count: Number of additional threads not shown, 1 or more. Not a plural ICU message in English; add plural forms if the language needs them

comments.reacted.meaning: Tooltip on an emoji reaction pill under a comment, naming who reacted with that emoji: up to three names, then the number of further people. The current user's name is replaced by 'You' (comments.mention-you).

placeholders.count: Total number of people who reacted with this emoji (selects the branch)
placeholders.a: Name of the first reactor, or 'You'
placeholders.others: Number of reactors beyond the first three, 1 or more

constraints: Verb must agree with a subject that may be 'You', one person, or several people
Keep all branches; nested plural on others

comments.reopen.meaning: Button in a resolved thread's header that marks the thread unresolved again (active again). Replaces 'Resolve' when the thread is resolved.
constraints: Button; keep short

comments.replies.meaning: Reply count shown on a thread row in the comments list and on thread hover previews, counting replies after the opening comment. Noun. Hidden when there are no replies.

comments.reply-placeholder.meaning: Placeholder in the text box at the bottom of an open thread for writing a reply. 'Reply' is an imperative verb inviting the user to reply.
constraints: Input placeholder; keep the trailing ellipsis character

comments.resolve.meaning: Button in a thread's header that marks the discussion as done/settled and hides it from the default view. 'Resolve' as in closing an issue, not solving a math problem or deciding. Paired with 'Reopen'.
constraints: Button; keep short

comments.resolved.meaning: Small tag on a thread row in the comments sidebar list indicating that thread has been marked resolved (done). Status adjective describing the thread.
constraints: Small badge; keep short

comments.resolved-by.meaning: Banner at the top of an open resolved thread saying who marked it resolved.

placeholders.name: Display name of the person who resolved the thread, or 'Someone' if unknown

comments.save.meaning: Submit button of the comment editor when editing an existing comment; saves the changed text.
constraints: Button; keep short

comments.see-less.meaning: Button under an expanded long comment that collapses it back to its truncated height. Paired with 'See more'.
constraints: Inline text button; keep short

comments.see-more.meaning: Button under a long comment that is cut off, expanding it to show the full text. Paired with 'See less'.
constraints: Inline text button; keep short

comments.send.meaning: Button that posts the comment or reply the user has typed into the comment composer, for a new comment thread or a reply in an existing thread. 'Send' means submit/post the message, not send by mail.
constraints: Short button label next to the text field

comments.show.meaning: Toggle that makes hidden comment pins visible on the canvas again. It alternates with a 'Hide comments' label depending on current state. 'Show' is an imperative command, not a noun (a show/display).

comments.show-all-pages.meaning: Checkbox item in the comments filter menu. When checked, the comments list includes comments from every page of the document, not only the current page.
constraints: Toggle (checkbox) menu item; keep short

comments.show-resolved.meaning: Checkbox item in the comments filter menu. When checked, comment threads that have been marked resolved (closed/done) are included in the list. 'Resolved' means a thread marked done, not a problem being solved or a decision.
constraints: Toggle (checkbox) menu item; keep short

comments.stack-label.meaning: Screen-reader label (aria-label) for a badge on the canvas that groups several comment threads pinned at the same location. Clicking it expands the stack. Says how many comment threads sit at that spot.

placeholders.count: Number of comment threads stacked at this canvas location, 2 or more in practice

comments.thread-title.meaning: Header shown at the top of an open comment thread panel. A noun naming the thread (a single comment), not the verb 'to comment'.
constraints: Singular noun

comments.title.meaning: Plural noun 'Comments'. Used as the header of the comments sidebar and as the label of a checkbox menu item (shortcut Shift+C) that turns comment visibility on or off. Noun, not the verb.

comments.unknown-author.meaning: Fallback name used in place of a person's display name when the author of a comment, reaction or resolution can't be found. It is inserted into other sentences (e.g. 'resolved by {name}', reaction summaries, pin labels), so it must work as the grammatical subject or name of a person.
constraints: Substituted into other messages as a person's name; avoid forms that only work standalone

confirm-open-link-dialog.cancel.meaning: Button in the 'Open external link?' confirmation dialog that closes the dialog without opening the link.

confirm-open-link-dialog.detail.meaning: Warning text in a confirmation dialog shown before opening a link that launches another application on the user's device (a non-web link, e.g. a custom app protocol). Tells the user to proceed only if they trust the link's source. The URL is shown below.

confirm-open-link-dialog.open.meaning: Primary button in the confirmation dialog that opens the link (in a new window/another app) and closes the dialog.

confirm-open-link-dialog.title.meaning: Title of a confirmation dialog asking whether the user really wants to open a link that leads outside the app (to another application on their device).

context-menu.arrange.meaning: Name of a submenu (in the context menu and as a command palette group) holding commands that position selected shapes: align, distribute, stack, bring forward/send backward, flip. 'Arrange' means lay out/organize shapes, not schedule or make an arrangement.
constraints: Submenu label; keep short

context-menu.copy-as.meaning: Submenu label; the submenu lists formats (SVG, PNG) to copy the selected shapes to the clipboard as. 'Copy' is the clipboard verb, not the noun 'a copy'. Followed visually by the format options.
constraints: Submenu label that leads into a list of file formats

context-menu.edit.meaning: Name of a context-menu submenu grouping commands that modify the selection: group/ungroup, flatten to image, frame selection, edit link, remove frame, convert to embed/bookmark, toggle auto size, lock. Corresponds to an 'Edit' menu, not a single 'edit this' action.
constraints: Submenu label; keep short

context-menu.export-all-as.meaning: Submenu label in the main menu; the submenu lists formats (SVG, PNG) to export all shapes on the current page to a file. Despite the key, the English is just 'Export'.
constraints: Submenu label; keep short

context-menu.export-as.meaning: Submenu label; the submenu lists file formats (SVG, PNG) to export the selected shapes to a downloaded file. Followed visually by the format options.
constraints: Submenu label that leads into a list of file formats

context-menu.move-to-page.meaning: Submenu label; the submenu lists the document's pages (plus 'New page') and moves the selected shapes to the chosen page. 'Page' is a page of the drawing document.
constraints: Submenu label that leads into a list of page names

context-menu.reorder.meaning: Tooltip and title on the drag handle beside each page in the page menu; dragging it changes the order of pages in the list. Means change the order, not place a new order/purchase.
constraints: Short tooltip

context-menu.title.meaning: Accessible name (aria-label) for the right-click context menu on the canvas, read by screen readers.

context.pages.new-page.meaning: Menu item that creates a new page in the document. In the 'Move to page' submenu it creates a new page and moves the selected shapes to it; in the command palette it creates and switches to a new page. 'New' is an adjective (a new page), not 'news'.

cursor-chat.type-to-chat.meaning: Placeholder text in the small chat input bubble attached to the user's cursor in multiplayer; whatever the user types appears next to their cursor for collaborators. Invites the user to start typing a message.
constraints: Input placeholder; keep the trailing ellipsis character

dash-style.dashed.meaning: Option in the style panel for a shape's stroke: a dashed line.
constraints: Adjective describing a line style; keep short

dash-style.dotted.meaning: Option in the style panel for a shape's stroke: a dotted line.
constraints: Adjective describing a line style; keep short

dash-style.draw.meaning: Option in the style panel for a shape's stroke: a hand-drawn, sketchy-looking line. A style name describing the line's look, not the verb 'to draw' and not the draw tool.
constraints: Sits alongside Solid/Dashed/Dotted as a line-style name; keep short

dash-style.solid.meaning: Option in the style panel for a shape's stroke: a continuous, unbroken line. 'Solid' as opposed to dashed/dotted, not as in solid matter or a filled shape.
constraints: Adjective describing a line style; keep short

document.default-name.meaning: Fallback name for a document without a name, used as the file name when exporting shapes to SVG or PNG. Describes the document as having no title.
constraints: Becomes part of a downloaded file name; avoid characters unsafe in file names

edit-link-dialog.cancel.meaning: Button in the 'Edit link' dialog that closes it without changing the shape's link.

edit-link-dialog.clear.meaning: Danger button in the 'Edit link' dialog, shown when the user has emptied the URL field of a shape that had a link. Removes the link from the shape and closes the dialog. Means remove the link, not tidy up or make transparent.

edit-link-dialog.detail.meaning: Help text under the URL field in the 'Edit link' dialog, explaining that clicking the shape's link opens it in a new browser tab.

edit-link-dialog.invalid-url.meaning: Inline error under the URL field of the Edit link dialog. It appears when the user presses Enter or Continue and what they typed isn't a usable web address. It replaces the hint 'Links will open in a new tab.' and goes away as soon as they type again.
constraints: Full sentence shown in place of a one-line hint; keep it about as short

edit-link-dialog.save.meaning: Primary button of the Edit link dialog. It saves the typed URL as the link on the selected shape and closes the dialog. Trap: the English says 'Continue', but the button confirms and saves. No further step follows, so don't translate it as 'go on to the next step'.
constraints: Dialog button; keep short

edit-link-dialog.title.meaning: Title of the dialog for adding or changing the hyperlink attached to the selected shape. 'Edit' is an imperative (edit the link), and 'link' means a web hyperlink.
constraints: Dialog title; keep short

edit-link-dialog.url.meaning: Label of the text field in the Edit link dialog where the user types the web address for the shape's link.
constraints: Field label; keep the locale's usual abbreviation for URL/web address

embed-dialog.back.meaning: Button in step 2 of the Insert embed dialog (entering a URL). It goes back to the list of embed services so the user can pick a different one. It means navigating back, not the back side of something.
constraints: Dialog button; keep short

embed-dialog.cancel.meaning: Button in the Insert embed dialog that closes the dialog without inserting anything.
constraints: Dialog button; keep short

embed-dialog.create.meaning: Primary button in the Insert embed dialog. It places an embed of the entered URL (for example a YouTube video or Figma file) at the centre of the canvas and closes the dialog. It stays disabled until the URL matches the chosen service.
constraints: Dialog button; keep short

embed-dialog.instruction.meaning: Hint under the URL field once the user has picked an embed service (YouTube, Figma, etc.), shown while the field is empty. It tells them to paste that site's link to create the embed. When the service has help docs, it is followed by a 'Learn more' link and a full stop.
constraints: A separate 'Learn more.' link may follow this sentence, so it must stand alone as a complete sentence

embed-dialog.invalid-url.meaning: Warning under the URL field in the Insert embed dialog. It appears shortly after the user stops typing if the URL can't be recognised as an embed for the chosen service.

embed-dialog.learn-more.meaning: Link after the paste-URL instruction in the Insert embed dialog. It opens the chosen service's help page about getting an embeddable link in a new tab. The UI adds a full stop after it.
constraints: Inline link; keep short; the UI appends a period after it

embed-dialog.title.meaning: Title of the dialog for inserting an embed (live content from another site, such as a video or design file) onto the canvas. After a service is picked it becomes 'Insert embed — <service name>'. 'Embed' is a noun here: the embedded item.
constraints: Dialog title; keep short; a service name is appended after an em dash

embed-dialog.url.meaning: Label of the text field in the Insert embed dialog where the user pastes the link to the content they want to embed.
constraints: Field label; keep the locale's usual abbreviation for URL/web address

error.cancel.meaning: Button in the 'Are you sure?' reset confirmation on the crash screen. It backs out of resetting and returns to the error message without deleting anything.
constraints: Button; keep short

error.confirm-reset.description.meaning: Warning in the confirmation step on the crash screen after the user clicks Reset data. It says that wiping the locally stored tldraw data deletes their drawing permanently.

error.confirm-reset.title.meaning: Heading of the confirmation step on the crash screen, asking the user to confirm they really want to reset their data.
constraints: Heading; keep short

error.copied.meaning: Tooltip and accessible label of the copy button on the crash screen for about two seconds after it copied the error details to the clipboard. It confirms that the copy happened. 'Copied' is a past participle about the action, not a noun meaning 'a copy'.
constraints: Icon-button tooltip and aria-label; keep short
