error.copy.meaning: Tooltip and accessible label of the icon button next to the error details on the crash screen. It copies the error message and stack trace to the clipboard. Trap: this is the verb (copy to the clipboard), not the noun 'a copy'.
constraints: Icon-button tooltip and aria-label; keep short

error.hide-details.meaning: Button on the crash screen that collapses the technical error details (message and stack trace) once they are showing.
constraints: Button; toggles with 'Show details'; keep the two parallel

error.message-label.meaning: Label that used to precede the error message text in the crash screen's technical details. The current UI no longer renders it, but the key is kept because apps may override it.
constraints: Label followed by a colon; keep the colon in the locale's style

error.note-label.meaning: Bold lead-in on the crash screen, followed by the warning that resetting erases the current project. 'Note' means 'please note' (an attention marker), not a sticky note or a musical note.
constraints: Inline bold label followed by a colon; the sentence 'Resetting will erase…' follows

error.refresh-hint.meaning: First sentence of the crash screen body, telling the user to reload the browser page. The reset hint follows it in the same paragraph.
constraints: Joined with following sentences in one paragraph; must be a complete sentence

error.refresh-page.meaning: Primary button on the crash screen that reloads the browser page. 'Refresh' means reload, not update the content.
constraints: Button; keep short

error.reset-data.meaning: Danger button on the crash screen. On the main view it opens a confirmation, and in that confirmation it wipes all tldraw data stored locally in the browser and reloads. 'Reset' means clearing the stored data back to empty, not restoring defaults or retrying.
constraints: Button used in two places with the same wording; keep short

error.reset-hint.meaning: Second sentence of the crash screen body. It says that if the problem continues after reloading, the user may need to clear the tldraw data saved locally in their browser or device. 'tldraw' is the product name.
constraints: Keep 'tldraw' untranslated and lowercase; part of one paragraph with the refresh hint

error.reset-note.meaning: Warning after the bold 'Note:' on the crash screen: resetting the data deletes the current project and any work not yet saved.
constraints: Follows the 'Note:' label in the same sentence flow

error.show-details.meaning: Button on the crash screen that expands the technical error details (message and stack trace) so the user can read or copy them.
constraints: Button; toggles with 'Hide details'; keep the two parallel

error.stack-trace-label.meaning: Label that used to precede the stack trace (the developer-facing list of code locations where the error happened) in the crash screen details. The current UI no longer renders it, but the key is kept for app overrides. 'Stack trace' is a programming term; many locales keep it as a loanword.
constraints: Label followed by a colon

error.title.meaning: Heading of the full-screen crash screen shown when the editor hits an unexpected error and can't continue.
constraints: Heading; no trailing punctuation

file-system.confirm-open.cancel.meaning: Button in the 'Overwrite current project?' dialog shown before opening a file. It closes the dialog and keeps the current project, without opening the file. The SDK declares this string, but host apps such as tldraw.com render it.
constraints: Dialog button; keep short

file-system.confirm-open.description.meaning: Body of the 'Overwrite current project?' dialog shown when the user opens a .tldr file. It warns that the opened file replaces what is on the canvas, that unsaved changes are lost, and asks whether to continue. The buttons are Cancel and 'Open file'.
constraints: Dialog body is narrow (about 350px wide)

file-system.confirm-open.open.meaning: Confirm button in the dialog shown on tldraw.com when a .tldr file is dropped onto a local (non-shared) board. Pressing it loads the file and replaces the current board's contents. 'Open' is a verb: open the file.
constraints: Dialog button; keep short
Destructive: replaces the current project and discards unsaved changes

file-system.confirm-open.title.meaning: Title of the confirmation dialog shown before a dropped .tldr file replaces the current board. Asks whether to overwrite (replace the contents of) the project currently open.
constraints: Dialog title phrased as a question
'Project' means the current board/document, not a software project

file-system.file-open-error.file-format-.meaning: Description in an error toast when a .tldr file cannot be loaded because it was saved by a newer tldraw version than the one running (or its migration targets a newer version). Tells the user to reload the page to get the latest version.
constraints: Toast body under the title 'Could not open file'

file-system.file-open-error.generic-corr.meaning: Description in an error toast when a .tldr file parses but its records are invalid or migrating it failed, i.e. the file's contents are damaged.
constraints: Toast body under the title 'Could not open file'

file-system.file-open-error.not-a-tldraw.meaning: Description in an error toast when the file the user tried to open could not be parsed as a tldraw (.tldr) file at all. 'tldraw' is the product name.
constraints: Toast body under the title 'Could not open file'
Keep 'tldraw' untranslated and lowercase

file-system.file-open-error.title.meaning: Title of the error toast shown when loading a .tldr file fails; the description below it gives the reason.
constraints: Toast title; keep short
Same English as file-system.shared-document-file-open-error.title; keep the two consistent

file-system.shared-document-file-open-er.meaning: Description in an error toast on tldraw.com when the user drops a .tldr file onto a shared (multiplayer) board: loading a file would replace a document other people are using, so it is refused.
constraints: Toast body
'Shared projects' means boards shared with collaborators

file-system.shared-document-file-open-er.meaning: Title of the error toast on tldraw.com when a .tldr file is dropped onto a shared (multiplayer) board and cannot be opened there.
constraints: Toast title; keep short
Same English as file-system.file-open-error.title; keep the two consistent

fill-style.fill.meaning: Name of a fill style value: the shape's interior is filled with a strong version of the shape's colour. Shown in the style panel's fill picker as 'Fill — Fill' style tooltips, in the command palette's style list, and as the label of the Alt+F keyboard-shortcut action that applies it. A noun naming a style, not the verb 'to fill'.
constraints: Appears after the picker title ('Fill — …'), so it must still read as a distinct option even though it repeats the category name
Keep distinct from Solid, Semi, Pattern and Lined fill

fill-style.lined-fill.meaning: Name of a fill style value: the shape is filled with colour and overlaid with lines (hatching). Shown in the style panel's fill picker, the command palette, and as the label of the Alt+Shift+F shortcut action.
constraints: Noun phrase naming a style; keep short
'Lined' means covered with drawn lines, not 'lined' as in a garment lining

fill-style.none.meaning: Fill style value meaning the shape has no fill: its interior is transparent and only the outline is drawn. Shown in the style panel's fill picker and command palette.
constraints: Refers to 'fill' (no fill); in gendered languages agree with the word for fill if needed

fill-style.pattern.meaning: Fill style value: the shape's interior is filled with a hatched/striped pattern in the shape's colour. Shown in the style panel's fill picker and command palette.
constraints: Noun naming a visual pattern, not a template or design pattern

fill-style.semi.meaning: Fill style value: the shape is filled with an opaque neutral (background-coloured, e.g. white) fill rather than its own colour. Short for 'semi' fill. Shown in the style panel's fill picker and command palette.
constraints: Ambiguous English: a truncated adjective ('semi'), not a truck; a short equivalent like 'semi' or 'partial' fill is fine
Keep very short

fill-style.solid.meaning: Fill style value: the shape's interior is filled with a light tint of the shape's colour. Shown in the style panel's fill picker and command palette.
constraints: Adjective describing a fill (not a solid object); agree with the word for fill if needed
Same English as dash-style.solid but here it modifies fill, not line

focus-mode.toggle-focus-mode.meaning: Tooltip of the small dot button shown while focus mode is on (all UI hidden). Clicking it turns focus mode off/on, bringing the menus and toolbars back.
constraints: Button title on an icon-only button; also its accessible name
'Toggle' means switch on/off

font-style.draw.meaning: Name of a font style value: tldraw's hand-drawn, handwriting-like font. Shown in the style panel's font picker and command palette.
constraints: Trap: not the verb 'draw' or the Draw tool; it names a hand-drawn typeface
Keep short; sits beside Sans, Serif and Mono

font-style.mono.meaning: Name of a font style value: a monospaced typeface. Shown in the style panel's font picker and command palette.
constraints: Typographic term (monospace), not mono audio or a monkey
Keep short

font-style.sans.meaning: Name of a font style value: a sans-serif typeface. Shown in the style panel's font picker and command palette.
constraints: Typographic term (sans-serif); keep short

font-style.serif.meaning: Name of a font style value: a serif typeface. Shown in the style panel's font picker and command palette.
constraints: Typographic term; keep short

geo-style.arrow-down.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a block arrow shape pointing downward. Shown in the style panel's geo dropdown and command palette, and announced by screen readers as the shape's name.
constraints: Noun phrase naming a shape: an arrow pointing down; 'down' is a direction, not a verb or command
Different from the arrow tool/connector

geo-style.arrow-left.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a block arrow shape pointing left. Shown in the style panel's geo dropdown and command palette, and announced by screen readers as the shape's name.
constraints: Noun phrase naming a shape: an arrow pointing left; 'left' is a direction, not the past tense of 'leave'

geo-style.arrow-right.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a block arrow shape pointing right. Shown in the style panel's geo dropdown and command palette, and announced by screen readers as the shape's name.
constraints: Noun phrase naming a shape: an arrow pointing right; 'right' is a direction, not 'correct'

geo-style.arrow-up.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a block arrow shape pointing upward. Shown in the style panel's geo dropdown and command palette, and announced by screen readers as the shape's name.
constraints: Noun phrase naming a shape: an arrow pointing up; 'up' is a direction

geo-style.check-box.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a square with a check mark inside (a ticked checkbox drawing). Shown in the style panel's geo dropdown and command palette, and announced by screen readers as the shape's name.
constraints: A shape name, not an interactive form checkbox and not the verb 'check'

geo-style.cloud.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a cloud outline. Shown in the style panel's geo dropdown and command palette, and announced by screen readers as the shape's name.
constraints: The weather-cloud shape, not cloud computing/storage

geo-style.diamond.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a diamond (a square rotated 45°, rhombus-like). Shown in the style panel's geo dropdown and command palette, and announced by screen readers as the shape's name.
constraints: Geometric shape, not the gemstone
Must stay distinct from geo-style.rhombus

geo-style.ellipse.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: an ellipse/oval-circle shape (the default round geo). Shown in the style panel's geo dropdown and command palette, and announced by screen readers as the shape's name.
constraints: Geometric term, not the punctuation ellipsis (…)
Must stay distinct from geo-style.oval

geo-style.heart.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a heart shape. Shown in the style panel's geo dropdown and command palette, and announced by screen readers as the shape's name.
constraints: The heart symbol shape, not the organ

geo-style.hexagon.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a six-sided polygon. Shown in the style panel's geo dropdown and command palette, and announced by screen readers as the shape's name.

geo-style.octagon.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: an eight-sided polygon. Shown in the style panel's geo dropdown and command palette, and announced by screen readers as the shape's name.

geo-style.oval.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: an oval (pill-like stretched ellipse). Shown in the style panel's geo picker and command palette, and announced to screen readers as the selected shape's name.
constraints: Noun naming a shape; keep short
Must stay distinct from 'Ellipse' (geo-style.ellipse)

geo-style.pentagon.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a five-sided polygon. Shown in the style panel's geo picker and command palette, and announced as the shape's name.
constraints: Noun naming a shape; keep short

geo-style.rectangle.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a rectangle (the default geo shape). Shown in the style panel's geo picker and command palette, and announced as the shape's name.
constraints: Noun naming a shape; keep short

geo-style.rhombus.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a rhombus/parallelogram leaning to the right. Shown in the style panel's geo picker and command palette, and announced as the shape's name.
constraints: Noun naming a shape; keep short
Must stay distinct from 'Diamond' (geo-style.diamond) and 'Rhombus left' (geo-style.rhombus-2)

geo-style.rhombus-2.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a rhombus/parallelogram leaning to the left, the mirror of 'Rhombus'. 'Left' is a direction describing the slant, not the past tense of 'leave'. Shown in the style panel's geo picker, command palette and a custom-menus example, and announced as the shape's name.
constraints: Noun phrase naming a shape; keep short
Must read as the same shape as 'Rhombus' with a leftward slant

geo-style.star.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a five-pointed star. Shown in the style panel's geo picker and command palette, and announced as the shape's name. The geometric figure, not a celebrity or a favourite/rating star.
constraints: Noun naming a shape; keep short

geo-style.trapezoid.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a trapezoid (four sides, one pair parallel, narrower at the top). Shown in the style panel's geo picker and command palette, and announced as the shape's name.
constraints: Noun naming a shape; keep short
Use the term for this quadrilateral in the locale (British 'trapezium' sense)

geo-style.triangle.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a triangle. Shown in the style panel's geo picker and command palette, and announced as the shape's name.
constraints: Noun naming a shape; keep short

geo-style.x-box.meaning: Name of a geo shape type: a rectangle with an X drawn corner to corner inside it (a crossed-out box). Shown in the style panel's geo picker and command palette, and announced as the shape's name. 'Box' means a square/rectangle, not a container or a TV/game console.
constraints: Noun phrase naming a shape; keep short
Parallels 'Check box' (geo-style.check-box)

help-menu.about.meaning: Help menu item that opens the tldraw about/website page.
constraints: 'tldraw' is a brand name; keep it lowercase and untranslated

help-menu.keyboard-shortcuts.meaning: Help menu item that opens the keyboard shortcuts dialog listing all shortcuts.
constraints: Menu item; use the locale's standard term for keyboard shortcuts

help-menu.privacy.meaning: Help menu link that opens tldraw's privacy policy page.
constraints: Use the locale's standard name for a legal privacy policy

help-menu.terms.meaning: Help menu link that opens tldraw's terms of service page.
constraints: Use the locale's standard name for legal terms of service

help-menu.title.meaning: Title of the help menu (the '?' button's menu) and of the matching group in the command palette, which holds keyboard shortcuts, about, privacy and terms links.
constraints: Also used as the help button's tooltip/accessible name; keep short

libraries.add-libraries.meaning: Button in the libraries panel that opens the browse dialog so the user can add more shape libraries to the current file. A library is a reusable collection of saved shapes/items.
constraints: Button label; keep short
'Library' means a collection of reusable shapes, not a code library or a building with books

libraries.add-selection.meaning: Accessible label (and hint) of a tile in a library that saves the currently selected shapes on the canvas into that library as a new item.
constraints: 'Selection' means the shapes currently selected on the canvas
Imperative/control form

libraries.add-to-library.meaning: Context menu and command palette submenu that saves the selected shapes into a library; its entries list existing libraries plus 'New library'. Also used in dotcom as a sign-in call to action.
constraints: Menu item that opens a submenu; keep short

libraries.add-to-new-library.meaning: Item inside the 'Add to library' submenu that creates a new library and saves the selected shapes into it.
constraints: Reads as a destination under 'Add to library'; 'New' describes the library, a noun phrase rather than a verb

libraries.back.meaning: Tooltip and accessible name of the chevron button in the browse libraries dialog that returns from viewing one library's items to the list of libraries.
constraints: Navigate back; not 'the back side' of something

libraries.browse-more.meaning: Command palette item that opens the browse libraries dialog to find and add more libraries to the file.
constraints: Command palette entry; keep short

libraries.browse.add.meaning: Button on a library row in the browse dialog that adds that library to the current file so its items show in the panel.
constraints: 'File' means the current tldraw document/board
Paired with 'Remove from file'; keep the two parallel

libraries.browse.add-error.title.meaning: Error toast title shown when adding a library to the file failed.
constraints: Toast title; short

libraries.browse.added.meaning: Status shown with a check icon on a library row in the browse dialog when that library is already added to the current file.
constraints: Refers to the library (masculine/feminine agreement may matter); status, not a button

libraries.browse.empty.meaning: Empty-state text in the browse libraries dialog when there are no libraries available to add.

libraries.browse.empty-library.meaning: Empty-state text shown for a library that has no items, in its row preview or when viewing it in the browse dialog.

libraries.browse.item-count.meaning: Detail line under a suggested library's name saying how many items it contains.

placeholders.count: Number of items in the library, 0 or more

libraries.browse.load-error.title.meaning: Title of an error message shown in the 'Browse libraries' dialog when the items of a library cannot be loaded for viewing, for example when the library's items fail to fetch. 'Items' are the saved shapes or templates stored in a library, not generic things.
constraints: Short error title; the contraction 'Couldn't' means a failure that already happened

libraries.browse.more.meaning: Compact overflow badge on the last thumbnail tile of a library's preview row, showing how many further items are not shown, e.g. '+ 3'.

placeholders.count: Number of hidden items, 1 or more

constraints: Very small tile; keep as a symbol plus number, no words
Screen readers get libraries.browse.more-label instead

libraries.browse.more-label.meaning: Accessible label of the '+ N' overflow tile in a library preview, read by screen readers to say how many more items the library has beyond those shown.

placeholders.count: Number of hidden items, 1 or more

libraries.browse.remove.meaning: Button on an already-added library row in the browse dialog (revealed on hover over 'Added') that removes the library from the current file. Does not delete the library itself.
constraints: Remove, not delete
Paired with 'Add to file'; keep parallel

libraries.browse.title.meaning: Title of the 'Browse libraries' dialog (or sheet view). It lists libraries the user can view, add to the current file or remove from it. 'Browse' means look through or explore, not a web browser.
constraints: Dialog title; keep short

libraries.browse.view.meaning: Accessible name (aria-label) for a library's name button in the Browse libraries dialog. Pressing it opens that library to show all its items. Screen-reader only; the visible text is just the library name.

placeholders.name: The library's name, as typed by its owner

constraints: Accessibility-only label, not shown on screen

libraries.command-palette.insert-from.meaning: Command palette submenu, one per library that has named items. It lists that library's items; picking one places the item on the canvas in the middle of the viewport. 'Insert' means place on the canvas.

placeholders.name: The library's name, as typed by its owner

libraries.command-palette.toggle-panel.meaning: Command palette command that opens the libraries panel if it is closed, or closes it if it is open. 'Toggle' means switch between shown and hidden.

libraries.copied.description.meaning: Description in the toast shown after something was copied. For an item, it names the library the item was copied into (the toast has an 'Open' button to go there). For a whole library, it names the owner (e.g. a team or workspace) the library was copied to.

placeholders.name: Name of the destination: a library when copying an item, or an owner (team/workspace) when copying a library

constraints: Avoid wording that only fits one of the two destination kinds

libraries.copied.title.meaning: Title of the success toast after an item or a library was duplicated into another library or owner. Past participle of 'copy' (it has been copied), not the clipboard and not the noun 'a copy'.
constraints: Toast title; keep to one word if possible

libraries.copy-error.title.meaning: Error toast title when copying a library item into another library failed.
constraints: Toast title; keep short

libraries.copy-name.meaning: Name given to the duplicate created when copying a library or a library item elsewhere: the original name followed by a marker that it is a copy. 'Copy' is the noun (a duplicate), not the verb.

placeholders.name: The original library's or item's name

constraints: Becomes stored data (the new name), so keep it short

libraries.delete-dialog.cancel.meaning: Button in the delete/remove confirmation dialog that closes it without deleting anything.
constraints: Button label; keep short

libraries.delete-dialog.confirm.meaning: Danger button in the confirmation dialog that permanently deletes the library or item. Unlike deleting shapes, this can't be undone.
constraints: Destructive action
Button label; keep short

libraries.delete-error.title.meaning: Error toast title when deleting a library item failed.
constraints: Toast title; keep short

libraries.delete-housed-library-dialog.b.meaning: Body of the confirmation dialog before deleting a library stored inside the current file, together with all its items. Deletion is permanent.

placeholders.name: The library's name
placeholders.count: Number of items in the library, 0 or more

constraints: Destructive action
Dialog max width about 350px

libraries.delete-item-dialog.body.meaning: Body of the confirmation dialog before permanently deleting a named item from a library.

placeholders.name: The item's name
placeholders.library: Name of the library the item is in

constraints: Destructive action
Dialog max width about 350px

libraries.delete-item-dialog.title.meaning: Title of the confirmation dialog before deleting a library item. 'Delete' is an imperative heading for the action.
constraints: Destructive action
Dialog title; keep short

libraries.delete-library-dialog.body.meaning: Body of the confirmation dialog before permanently deleting a library and every item in it.

placeholders.name: The library's name
placeholders.count: Number of items in the library, 0 or more

constraints: Destructive action
Dialog max width about 350px

libraries.delete-library-dialog.title.meaning: Title of the confirmation dialog before deleting a whole library.
constraints: Destructive action
Dialog title; keep short

libraries.delete-unnamed-item-dialog.bod.meaning: Body of the confirmation dialog before permanently deleting a library item that has no name.

placeholders.library: Name of the library the item is in

constraints: Destructive action
Dialog max width about 350px

libraries.empty.meaning: Placeholder shown in the libraries panel when the user has no libraries.

libraries.empty-library.meaning: Placeholder shown in the libraries panel when the open library contains no items.

libraries.item-details.created.meaning: Field label in an item's Details dialog. The value next to it is the date the item was created (saved to the library).
constraints: Label in a two-column term/value list; keep short
Value is a formatted date (libraries.item-details.saved-on)

libraries.item-details.created-by.meaning: Field label in an item's Details dialog. The value next to it is the display name of the person who created the item.
constraints: Label in a two-column term/value list; keep short

libraries.item-details.library.meaning: Field label in an item's Details dialog. The value next to it is the name of the library the item belongs to. A library here is a collection of reusable shapes, not a building or a code library.
constraints: Label in a two-column term/value list; keep short

libraries.item-details.name.meaning: Field label in an item's Details dialog. The value next to it is the item's name, which can be clicked to rename it.
constraints: Label in a two-column term/value list; keep short

libraries.item-details.saved-on.meaning: The creation date shown as the value of the 'Created on' field in an item's Details dialog. The message is just an ICU date format with nothing to translate; the locale formats the date itself.

placeholders.date: Timestamp when the item was created, shown in medium date format

constraints: Keep the ICU '{date, date, medium}' exactly; only reorder or add text if the locale truly requires it

libraries.item-details.title.meaning: Title of the dialog showing a library item's preview and information (name, library, creation date, creator). 'Details' is a noun: information about the item.
constraints: Dialog title; keep short

libraries.item-menu.copy-to.meaning: Submenu in a library item's menu listing other libraries; choosing one duplicates the item into that library, leaving the original where it is. Not the clipboard.
constraints: Menu item that opens a list of destination libraries; keep short
Must stay distinct from 'Move to'

libraries.item-menu.delete.meaning: Menu item in a library item's menu that asks for confirmation and then permanently deletes the item from the library.
constraints: Destructive action
Menu item; keep short

libraries.item-menu.details.meaning: Menu item in a library item's menu that opens the item's Details dialog (preview, name, library, creation date, creator). 'Details' is the noun, used as a menu command to show them.
constraints: Menu item; keep short

libraries.item-menu.insert.meaning: Menu item in a library item's menu (in the libraries panel) that places the item's shapes on the canvas, as clicking its tile does.
constraints: Menu item; keep short

libraries.item-menu.move-to.meaning: Submenu in a library item's menu listing other libraries; choosing one moves the item there, removing it from its current library.
constraints: Menu item that opens a list of destination libraries; keep short
Must stay distinct from 'Copy to'

libraries.item-menu.rename.meaning: Menu item in a library item's ⋯ / right-click menu. Starts editing the item's name in place wherever the name is shown. 'Rename' is a verb (command), not the noun 'new name'.
constraints: Short dropdown menu item
Applies to one item (a saved shape/snippet), not a library; keep separate from libraries.library-menu.rename only if the language needs a different object

libraries.item-menu.title.meaning: Tooltip and accessible title of the ⋯ icon button on a library item tile that opens its menu (Insert, Details, Rename, Move to, Copy to, Delete). 'Options' means the menu of actions for this item, not settings or preferences.
constraints: Tooltip on an icon button; keep short
'Item' is one entry in a library (a saved set of shapes)

libraries.item-order.default.meaning: Option in the library 'Sort by' submenu: keep items in the source's own order (no sorting). 'Default' names the original/standard order, not a default value setting.
constraints: Checkable menu item under 'Sort by'; should read naturally as a sort order
Single word preferred

libraries.item-order.name.meaning: Option in the library 'Sort by' submenu: sort items alphabetically A to Z by their name; unnamed items last. 'Name' is the noun (the item's name), not the verb 'to name'.
constraints: Checkable menu item under 'Sort by'; reads as 'Sort by > Name'
Single word preferred

libraries.item-order.newest.meaning: Option in the library 'Sort by' submenu: sort items newest first by when they were saved. Refers to items (plural, implied), as in 'newest first'.
constraints: Checkable menu item under 'Sort by'; reads as 'Sort by > Newest'
Single word preferred; if the language needs gender/number agreement, it refers to the library's items

libraries.library-error.title.meaning: Error toast title shown when an operation on a library fails: renaming, deleting, removing it from the file, copying it, creating a new library, or removing it in the Browse libraries dialog. 'Change' means modify/update the library generically, not swap it for another library.
constraints: Toast title; short
Trap: 'change' is not 'switch/replace'; it is a generic 'could not update' failure

libraries.library-menu.add-to-document.meaning: Menu item in a library's ⋯ menu that makes the library show in the current tldraw file (attaches it to this document) so its items are available there. Does not copy the library's items onto the canvas.
constraints: Short menu item
'File' means the current tldraw document/board, not a computer file on disk
Opposite of libraries.library-menu.remove-from-document

libraries.library-menu.copy.meaning: Submenu label in a library's ⋯ menu; the submenu lists owners (e.g. the user or a team/workspace) and choosing one duplicates the whole library to that owner. 'Copy' is the verb; 'to' introduces the destination chosen in the submenu.
constraints: Submenu label followed by a list of destination names; should read as 'Copy to → <owner>'
Not the clipboard copy; it duplicates the library
Keep distinct from moving

libraries.library-menu.create.meaning: Menu item in a library's ⋯ menu that creates a new, empty library. Shown only when the host passes onCreate. Command, read as 'create a new library'.
constraints: Short menu item
Same English as libraries.new-library-name, but this one is an action label, not a default name

libraries.library-menu.delete.meaning: Menu item at the bottom of a library's ⋯ menu that permanently deletes the library and its items, after a confirmation dialog.
constraints: Destructive action
Keep distinct from 'Remove from file', which only detaches the library from this file without deleting it

libraries.library-menu.remove-from-docum.meaning: Menu item in a library's ⋯ menu that stops showing the library in the current tldraw file, without deleting the library itself. Opens a confirmation dialog first.
constraints: 'File' means the current tldraw document/board
Must not read as delete; the library still exists elsewhere
Opposite of libraries.library-menu.add-to-document

libraries.library-menu.rename.meaning: Menu item in a library's ⋯ menu that starts editing the library's name in its header. Also the hover title of a library's name in the Browse libraries dialog, where double-clicking the name renames it. Verb (command).
constraints: Short menu item / tooltip
Applies to a library

libraries.library-menu.reverse.meaning: Checkable toggle at the end of the 'Sort by' submenu that reverses the chosen sort order of the library's items (e.g. oldest first, Z to A). Checked when reversed.
constraints: Checkbox menu item inside 'Sort by'; reads as an on/off option
Short

libraries.library-menu.sort.meaning: Submenu label in the libraries ⋯ menus; the submenu lists ways to order the items (Default, Newest, Name) plus 'Reverse order'. Read as 'Sort by → <criterion>'.
constraints: Submenu label followed by the sort criteria; options are nouns/adjectives (Default, Newest, Name)
'Sort' means order/arrange, not 'kind/type'

libraries.library-menu.title.meaning: Tooltip and accessible title of the ⋯ icon button that opens a library's menu (rename, sort, copy, add/remove from file, delete); also the libraries panel header's ⋯ menu. 'Options' means the menu of actions, not settings.
constraints: Tooltip on an icon button; keep short

libraries.move-error.title.meaning: Error toast title shown when moving a library item to another library (via the item menu's 'Move to') fails.
constraints: Toast title; short
'Item' is one entry in a library

libraries.moved.description.meaning: Description in the success toast after an item was moved to another library, naming the destination library.

placeholders.name: Name of the library the item was moved into (user-defined text)

constraints: The subject (the item) is implied; if the language needs it explicit or needs agreement, it is one library item
Library names are arbitrary user text, so avoid case endings that would require inflecting {name}

libraries.moved.open.meaning: Primary button on the success toast after an item was moved or copied to another library. Opens the libraries panel showing the destination library.
constraints: Toast button; very short
Verb (open/show the library), not the adjective 'open'

libraries.moved.title.meaning: Title of the success toast shown after a library item was moved to another library. Past participle describing the item ('the item was moved'), not the noun 'move'.
constraints: Toast title; one word ideally
If agreement is needed, it refers to one item

libraries.new-library-name.meaning: Default name given to a freshly created library (numbered 'New library 2' etc. if taken). Becomes the library's actual name, which the user can then edit. Noun phrase, not a command.
constraints: Used as a data value (stored name), so a plain noun phrase
A number may be appended after it
Same English as libraries.library-menu.create, which is the action

libraries.panel.add-library.meaning: Menu item in the libraries panel header's ⋯ menu that opens the Browse libraries dialog, where the user picks existing libraries to add to the current file. Does not create a new library.
constraints: Short menu item
Keep distinct from 'Create library' (makes a new one)

libraries.panel.create-library.meaning: Creates a new, empty library. Menu item in the libraries panel header's ⋯ menu and a button in the Browse libraries dialog footer; when there are several possible owners it opens a submenu of owners to create it for.
constraints: Short menu item / button
Keep distinct from 'Add library' (attach an existing one)

libraries.panel.this-file.meaning: Accessible name (aria-label) of the group in the libraries panel that holds the libraries attached to or stored in the current tldraw file.
constraints: Screen-reader only (aria-label), not shown visually
'File' means the current tldraw document/board

libraries.place-error.title.meaning: Error toast title shown when inserting a library item onto the canvas fails (clicking its tile or choosing Insert). 'Place' means put the item's shapes on the canvas.
constraints: Toast title; short
'Place' is not a noun 'location'

libraries.remove-library-dialog.body.meaning: Question in the confirmation dialog shown before removing a library from the current file. The library itself is not deleted; it just stops showing in this file.

placeholders.name: The library's name (user-defined text), shown inside curly quotes

constraints: Keep the quotes around {name}; use the locale's quotation marks if appropriate
'File' means the current tldraw document/board
Must not suggest deletion

libraries.remove-library-dialog.confirm.meaning: Confirm button of the dialog that removes a library from the current file (without deleting it).
constraints: Dialog button; short
Should match the remove (not delete) wording of the dialog title and libraries.library-menu.remove-from-document

libraries.remove-library-dialog.title.meaning: Title of the confirmation dialog shown before removing a library from the current file. Removing detaches the library from this file; it is not deleted.
constraints: Dialog heading; short
'File' means the current tldraw document/board
Keep distinct from the delete-library dialog

libraries.rename-error.title.meaning: Error toast title shown when saving a new name for a library item fails.
constraints: Toast title; short
'Item' is one entry in a library

libraries.save-error.title.meaning: Error toast title shown when saving the selected shapes into a library as a new item fails. 'Save to library' means add the selection to a library.
constraints: Toast title; short
Not saving the file/document

libraries.save-to-new-library-error.titl.meaning: Error toast title shown when 'save selection to a new library' fails: creating the new library (named 'New library') and saving the selected shapes into it.
constraints: Toast title; short

libraries.saved.description.meaning: Body of the confirmation toast shown after the selected shapes were saved as an item into a library while the libraries panel was closed. 'Added' means the selection was added to that library.

placeholders.name: The user-chosen name of the library the item was saved to

constraints: Toast body; short sentence

libraries.saved.open.meaning: Primary button in the 'Added to library' toast. Opens the libraries panel showing the library the item was just saved to. Verb 'open', not the adjective.
constraints: Toast button; keep very short

libraries.saved.title.meaning: Title of the confirmation toast after the user saved their selected shapes into a library (shown only when the libraries panel is closed). Past-tense confirmation, not an instruction.
constraints: Toast title; short

libraries.search.clear.meaning: Accessible label/tooltip of the button in the libraries search field that empties the search query. 'Clear' means erase the text, not 'transparent'.
constraints: Icon button label; short

libraries.search.label.meaning: Accessible label of the search field in the libraries panel, which filters items across the user's libraries.

libraries.search.no-results.meaning: Empty-state text in the libraries panel when a search or item filter matches no library items.

libraries.search.placeholder.meaning: Placeholder text inside the libraries panel search field. 'Search' is the imperative/invitation to search, with an ellipsis.
constraints: Placeholder in a narrow field; keep very short; keep the ellipsis character

libraries.search.searching.meaning: Loading text in the libraries panel while search results are being fetched. 'Searching' is an ongoing state.
constraints: Keep the ellipsis character

libraries.select-to-add.meaning: Tooltip (and accessible description) of the disabled + tile in a library when nothing is selected on the canvas: tells the user to select shapes on the canvas so they can add them to this library as an item.
constraints: Tooltip; short; 'them' refers to the shapes

libraries.sheet.close.meaning: Close button of the libraries panel when it is shown as a bottom sheet on phones. Visually hidden; only for screen readers. Closes the libraries panel.
constraints: Screen-reader-only text

libraries.sheet.resize.meaning: Accessible label of the drag handle at the top of the libraries bottom sheet on phones; tapping or dragging it switches the sheet between half and full height. 'Resize' the sheet, not the libraries' content.
constraints: Screen-reader-only label

libraries.this-file.add.meaning: Button next to a suggested library under 'Suggested libraries' that adds that library to the current file. Also prefixes the library name in its accessible label ('Add <library name>').
constraints: Small button; keep very short
Accessible label is this word followed by the library name, so it must read naturally before a name

libraries.this-file.empty.meaning: Empty-state text on the 'This file' view of the libraries panel when no libraries have been added to the current file yet.

libraries.this-file.suggested.meaning: Heading (and section label) above a short list of libraries offered to add to the current file, shown when it has none yet.

libraries.title.meaning: Name of the Libraries feature: collections of reusable saved shapes/items. Used as the libraries panel title, its toolbar/quick-action button label, the phone sheet title, and a command palette group heading. Not book libraries or code libraries.
constraints: Panel title and button label; keep short

libraries.too-new.description.meaning: Body of an error toast when a library item can't be loaded because it was created by a newer tldraw version; reloading the page gets the newer version. 'Reload' means refresh the page/app.
constraints: 'tldraw' is the product name; leave untranslated

libraries.too-new.title.meaning: Title of the error toast shown when a library item's content was made with a newer version of tldraw than the one running, so it can't be used.
constraints: 'tldraw' is the product name; leave untranslated
Toast title

libraries.unnamed-item.meaning: Fallback name for a library item that has no name, used as its accessible label in item grids and as its name in the item details dialog.

menu.accessibility.meaning: Name of the Accessibility submenu in the main menu's preferences and of the matching submenu in the command palette's Preferences group; contains accessibility settings.
constraints: Menu label; referred to by other strings like 'Preferences > Accessibility'

menu.edit.meaning: Name of the Edit submenu in the main menu (undo, cut, copy, etc.) and of the Edit group heading in the command palette. Standard 'Edit' menu name, not a verb on a specific item.
constraints: Menu name; use the locale's conventional application menu name

menu.input-device.meaning: Name of the submenu in the preferences where the user chooses whether they navigate with a mouse or a trackpad (or auto).
constraints: Menu label; short

menu.language.meaning: Name of the submenu listing interface languages the user can switch tldraw's UI to.
constraints: Menu label; short

menu.preferences.meaning: Name of the Preferences submenu in the main menu and the Preferences group heading in the command palette; holds user settings.
constraints: Menu label; referred to by other strings like 'Preferences > Accessibility'

menu.theme.meaning: Name of the submenu where the user picks the colour scheme: light, dark or system.
constraints: Menu label; short

menu.title.meaning: Tooltip/title of the hamburger button that opens tldraw's main menu. The noun 'menu'.
constraints: Icon button tooltip; one word

menu.view.meaning: Name of the View submenu in the main menu (zoom, grid, etc.) and the View group heading in the command palette. Noun as in the standard 'View' application menu, not the verb 'to view'.
constraints: Menu name; use the locale's conventional application menu name

navigation-zone.minimap.meaning: Accessible label of the minimap canvas: a small overview image of the whole board in the navigation panel.
constraints: Screen-reader label

navigation-zone.title.meaning: Accessible label of the navigation toolbar in the bottom corner holding the zoom menu and minimap controls.
constraints: Screen-reader toolbar label

navigation-zone.toggle-minimap.meaning: Tooltip of the button in the navigation panel that shows or hides the minimap.
constraints: Icon button tooltip; short

navigation-zone.zoom.meaning: Noun 'zoom' (the zoom level), used in the zoom menu button's tooltip and accessible label as 'Zoom — 100%' followed by the current percentage. Not the imperative 'zoom in'.
constraints: Followed in code by ' — ' and a percentage; keep short

opacity-style.0.1.meaning: Name of the 10% opacity setting, picked from the opacity slider in the style panel. It sets how see-through the selected shapes are. 10% is the most transparent option.
constraints: Use the locale's percentage format (number, spacing and % sign position)

opacity-style.0.25.meaning: Name of the 25% opacity setting, picked from the opacity slider in the style panel. It sets how see-through the selected shapes are.
constraints: Use the locale's percentage format (number, spacing and % sign position)

opacity-style.0.5.meaning: Name of the 50% opacity setting, picked from the opacity slider in the style panel. It sets how see-through the selected shapes are.
constraints: Use the locale's percentage format (number, spacing and % sign position)

opacity-style.0.75.meaning: Name of the 75% opacity setting, picked from the opacity slider in the style panel. It sets how see-through the selected shapes are.
constraints: Use the locale's percentage format (number, spacing and % sign position)

opacity-style.1.meaning: Name of the 100% opacity setting, picked from the opacity slider in the style panel. At 100% the shapes are fully opaque.
constraints: Use the locale's percentage format (number, spacing and % sign position)

page-menu.create-new-page.meaning: Label of the button in the page menu that adds a new page to the document. It is also the title of the browser prompt that asks for the new page's name on devices where the prompt is used.
constraints: Button label/tooltip; keep short

page-menu.go-to-page.meaning: Tooltip on each page row in the page list. Clicking the row switches the canvas to that page. 'Go to' means navigate, not move something.

page-menu.max-pages-reached.meaning: Replaces the 'Create new page' button label when the document already has the maximum number of pages allowed, so no more can be added.
constraints: Shown in place of a button label; keep short

page-menu.new-page-initial-name.meaning: Default name given to a newly created page, from the page menu, the command palette or 'move to new page'. If the name is already taken, the trailing number is incremented (Page 2, Page 3…).
constraints: Must end with the digit 1. Auto-incrementing only works on a number at the very end of the string, so put the word before the number

page-menu.resize.meaning: Accessible name (aria-label) of the drag handle that resizes the height of the page list in the page menu. Screen readers only.

page-menu.submenu.delete.meaning: Item in a page's submenu in the page list that deletes that page.

page-menu.submenu.duplicate-page.meaning: Item in a page's submenu in the page list that makes a copy of the page and all its contents. 'Duplicate' is a verb (a command), not the noun 'a duplicate'.
constraints: Keep distinct from 'Copy' (clipboard)

page-menu.submenu.move-down.meaning: Item in a page's submenu that moves the page one position down in the page order.

page-menu.submenu.move-up.meaning: Item in a page's submenu that moves the page one position up in the page order.

page-menu.submenu.rename.meaning: Item in a page's submenu that starts editing the page's name.

page-menu.submenu.title.meaning: Tooltip on the '…' icon button next to each page in the page list. The button opens that page's options menu. 'Menu' is a noun.

page-menu.title.meaning: Heading of the 'Pages' group in the command palette, which lists the document's pages to switch to. Pages are the separate canvases in one document, not web pages.

people-menu.anonymous-user.meaning: Placeholder display name shown in the people menu for a collaborator, or for yourself, who hasn't set a name.
constraints: Used as a person's name; 'New' means newly joined/unnamed, not a 'new account' signup

people-menu.avatar-color.meaning: Accessible label of the coloured dot next to a collaborator's name in the people menu. It shows the cursor/avatar colour assigned to that person.

people-menu.change-color.meaning: Tooltip on the colour button next to your own name in the people menu. It opens a picker to choose your cursor/avatar colour.

people-menu.change-name.meaning: Tooltip on the edit button next to your own name in the people menu. It lets you edit the display name other collaborators see.

people-menu.follow.meaning: Tooltip on the button next to a collaborator in the people menu. Clicking it makes your viewport follow theirs live, so you see what they see on the canvas. Not following on social media.

people-menu.following.meaning: Tooltip on the follow button when your viewport is already following this collaborator's view. Clicking it again stops following. Not a social-media follow.

people-menu.leading.meaning: Tooltip on the follow button when this collaborator is following your viewport, so their view tracks what you see. Not a social-media follow.

people-menu.title.meaning: Tooltip on the button of collaborator avatars in the top bar. It opens the menu listing the people currently in the document.

people-menu.user.meaning: Small tag shown after your own placeholder name in the people menu, marking that entry as you.
constraints: Keep the parentheses (or the locale's equivalent)

shortcuts-dialog.a11y.meaning: Heading of the accessibility group in the keyboard shortcuts dialog. The group lists shortcuts such as moving the selection between shapes with the keyboard.

shortcuts-dialog.collaboration.meaning: Heading of the collaboration group in the keyboard shortcuts dialog. It lists multiplayer shortcuts such as opening cursor chat.

shortcuts-dialog.disabled-notice.meaning: Notice at the top of the keyboard shortcuts dialog when the user has turned keyboard shortcuts off. It tells them where to turn them back on.
constraints: 'Preferences > Accessibility' names real menu labels: use this locale's translations of the menu keys for Preferences and Accessibility, keeping the '>' separator

shortcuts-dialog.edit.meaning: Heading of the editing group in the keyboard shortcuts dialog (undo, redo, cut, copy, paste and so on). It is the category name, like an Edit menu, not a command to edit something.

shortcuts-dialog.preferences.meaning: Group heading in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog over the shortcuts for user preference toggles (dark mode, focus mode, grid).
constraints: Should match the locale's name for the app's Preferences menu

shortcuts-dialog.text-formatting.meaning: Group heading in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog over the rich-text formatting shortcuts (bold, italic, code, highlight).

shortcuts-dialog.title.meaning: Title of the dialog that lists all keyboard shortcuts.

shortcuts-dialog.tools.meaning: Group heading in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog over the shortcuts that pick drawing tools (select, draw, eraser, rectangle, arrow, etc.).
constraints: Plural noun: the canvas tools, not 'utilities' or a toolbox

shortcuts-dialog.transform.meaning: Group heading in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog over shortcuts that rearrange selected shapes: reorder (bring to front/send back), group/ungroup, frame, lock, flip, align and distribute.
constraints: Heading noun for a category, not an imperative 'transform this'

shortcuts-dialog.view.meaning: Group heading in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog over zoom shortcuts (zoom in/out, to 100%, to fit, to selection). 'View' as in the camera/viewport menu.
constraints: Noun (the View menu), not the verb 'to look at'

size-style.l.meaning: Value of the Size style: large. Controls stroke thickness and text size of selected shapes. Shown as a picker button tooltip ('Size — Large') and in the command palette.
constraints: Adjective describing the size; keep parallel with Small/Medium/Extra large

size-style.m.meaning: Value of the Size style: medium. Controls stroke thickness and text size of selected shapes.
constraints: Adjective for size, not 'medium' as in a material or channel

size-style.s.meaning: Value of the Size style: small. Controls stroke thickness and text size of selected shapes.

size-style.xl.meaning: Value of the Size style: extra large, the biggest option. Controls stroke thickness and text size of selected shapes.

spline-style.cubic.meaning: Value of the line shape's Spline style: the line is drawn as a smooth cubic curve through its points.
constraints: Mathematical term (cubic curve), not a unit of volume

spline-style.line.meaning: Value of the line shape's Spline style: straight segments between points (polyline), as opposed to Cubic curves.
constraints: Means straight/segmented, contrasted with a curve; not a line of text

status.offline.meaning: Tooltip and icon label of the indicator shown when the connection to the sync server is lost.
constraints: Status adjective; keep short

style-panel.align.meaning: Name of the text alignment control in the style panel (start/middle/end/justify for text shapes); used as tooltip prefix, toolbar label and accessible subheading.
constraints: Setting name, not a command; keep short

style-panel.arrow-kind.meaning: Name of the arrow-type dropdown in the style panel, choosing how an arrow's path runs: Arc (curved) or Elbow (right-angled). Also a command palette group label.
constraints: English says 'Line' but it means the arrow's path/route type; not the line tool or a line of text

style-panel.arrowhead-end.meaning: Label of the dropdown choosing the arrowhead at the end (tip) of an arrow; appears as 'End — Triangle' in tooltips.
constraints: Noun: the end point of the arrow, not the verb 'to end'

style-panel.arrowhead-start.meaning: Label of the dropdown choosing the arrowhead at the start (tail) of an arrow; appears as 'Start — None' in tooltips.
constraints: Noun: the starting point of the arrow, not the verb 'to start'

style-panel.arrowheads.meaning: Name of the style panel control pairing the start and end arrowhead pickers of an arrow.
constraints: Means arrowheads (the tips), not arrow shapes

style-panel.color.meaning: Name of the color picker in the style panel; prefixes each swatch tooltip ('Color — Blue').

style-panel.dash.meaning: Name of the stroke pattern picker in the style panel (draw, solid, dashed, dotted).
constraints: Line/stroke style, not the punctuation mark or 'to rush'

style-panel.fill.meaning: Name of the fill picker in the style panel choosing how a shape's interior is filled (none, semi, solid, pattern…).
constraints: Noun (the fill style), not an imperative

style-panel.font.meaning: Name of the font family picker in the style panel (draw, sans, serif, mono).

style-panel.geo.meaning: Name of the dropdown in the style panel that changes a geo shape's type (rectangle, ellipse, star…).
constraints: Geometric shape/form, not condition ('in good shape')

style-panel.label-align.meaning: Name of the control setting horizontal (and vertical) alignment of a shape's text label, e.g. text inside a rectangle or on an arrow. Also a command palette group label.
constraints: Setting name ('label alignment'), not a command

style-panel.mixed.meaning: Shown in a style picker or the opacity slider when the selected shapes have different values for that style.
constraints: Means 'various/multiple values', not 'blended together'

style-panel.opacity.meaning: Name of the opacity slider in the style panel (10%–100%); its tooltip and accessible subheading.

style-panel.position.meaning: Style panel section name for position. No default picker uses it; available as a heading for a custom style panel section via stylePanelMessageId.
constraints: Noun: placement on the canvas

style-panel.selected.meaning: Appended in parentheses to the active option of a style picker, in its tooltip and aria-label, e.g. 'Color — Blue (selected)'.
constraints: Lowercase, mid-phrase; the subject is the style option, so agree in gender/number accordingly or use a neutral form

style-panel.size.meaning: Name of the size picker in the style panel (S, M, L, XL), which sets stroke thickness and text size.

style-panel.spline.meaning: Name of the dropdown choosing how a line shape is drawn between its points: Line (straight segments) or Cubic (smooth curve).
constraints: Technical curve term (spline); a native term for curve type is fine

style-panel.title.meaning: Title of the panel that shows style options (color, fill, dash, size, font and so on) for the selected shapes. Shown as the mobile style panel's title and as the group heading for style commands in the command palette. 'Styles' means visual formatting, not fashion or writing style.
constraints: Short panel heading

style-panel.vertical-align.meaning: Name of the style setting that controls where a geo shape's text label sits vertically inside the shape (top, middle or bottom). Used as the tooltip of the vertical-alignment picker button in the style panel, as that picker's heading, and as a command palette entry. 'Align' here is a noun-like setting name, not a command.
constraints: Icon button tooltip and section heading; keep short

theme.dark.meaning: Checkbox option in the Theme submenu that switches the editor to the dark color scheme. Refers to the color scheme (dark mode), an adjective describing the theme.
constraints: Menu item next to 'Light' and 'System'; agree grammatically with the locale's word for theme/color scheme if needed

theme.light.meaning: Checkbox option in the Theme submenu that switches the editor to the light color scheme. 'Light' means pale/bright (light mode), not lightweight and not a lamp.
constraints: Menu item next to 'Dark' and 'System'

theme.system.meaning: Checkbox option in the Theme submenu that makes the editor follow the operating system's light/dark setting. Means 'use the system setting', not a generic 'system'.
constraints: Menu item next to 'Light' and 'Dark'; keep short

toast.close.meaning: Button on a toast notification that dismisses it. Used when the toast doesn't supply its own close label.
constraints: Small button; keep short
Use the locale's standard verb for closing/dismissing a notification

toast.error.meaning: Accessible label of the icon on a toast with error severity, read by screen readers to convey the toast's kind. Noun: 'an error'.
constraints: Not visible text; icon label only
Keep parallel with toast.success, toast.info, toast.warning

toast.error.copy-fail.desc.meaning: Description of the warning toast shown when copying the selected shapes to the clipboard as an image (SVG/PNG via 'Copy as') fails.
constraints: 'Copy' is copying to the clipboard, not making a duplicate

toast.error.copy-fail.title.meaning: Title of the warning toast shown when copying shapes to the clipboard as an image fails. Terse English meaning 'Copy failed'; 'copy' is the clipboard action, not the noun 'a copy'.
constraints: Toast title; keep short
Trap: not 'a failed copy' (a defective duplicate) — it means the copy operation failed

toast.error.export-fail.desc.meaning: Description of the toast shown when exporting the selected shapes or page as an image file (SVG, PNG, etc.) fails.

toast.error.export-fail.title.meaning: Title of the toast shown when exporting shapes as an image file fails. Terse English meaning 'Export failed'.
constraints: Toast title; keep short
Means the export operation failed, not a defective exported item

toast.info.meaning: Accessible label of the icon on a toast with info severity, read by screen readers. Short for 'information'.
constraints: Not visible text; icon label only
Keep parallel with toast.success, toast.warning, toast.error

toast.moved-to-page.action.meaning: Button on the toast shown after moving shapes to another page via 'Move to page'; clicking it returns the user to the page they were on before.
constraints: Primary button inside a toast; keep short
Navigates back to the previous page; it does not undo the move

toast.moved-to-page.desc.meaning: Toast description after the user moves the selected shapes to another page; the editor also switches to that page. Says where the shapes (and the user) went.

placeholders.page: Name of the destination page, user-defined text such as 'Page 2'

constraints: The subject (the shapes) is implicit in English; the locale may need an explicit or neutral subject

toast.moved-to-page.title.meaning: Title of the toast shown after moving shapes to another page: tells the user they are now viewing a different page.
constraints: Toast title; keep short
Trap: 'Changed' means switched to another page, not that a page was modified/edited

toast.success.meaning: Accessible label of the icon on a toast with success severity, read by screen readers.
constraints: Not visible text; icon label only
Keep parallel with toast.info, toast.warning, toast.error

toast.warning.meaning: Accessible label of the icon on a toast with warning severity, read by screen readers. Noun: 'a warning'.
constraints: Not visible text; icon label only
Keep parallel with toast.success, toast.info, toast.error

tool-panel.more.meaning: Tooltip and label of the overflow button at the end of the main toolbar that opens a popover with the tools that didn't fit (e.g. more shapes). Means 'more tools'.
constraints: Small toolbar button; keep very short

tool-panel.title.meaning: Accessible label of the main toolbar that holds the drawing tools (select, hand, draw, shapes, etc.).
constraints: Plural noun naming the toolbar

tool.arrow.meaning: Name of the arrow tool, which draws connector arrows between points or shapes. Noun naming the tool.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short
Distinct from the arrow-shaped geo shapes (tool.arrow-up etc.)

tool.arrow-down.meaning: Name of a geo shape: a block arrow pointing downward. 'Down' is the direction it points, not a verb or a keyboard key.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short
Keep consistent with the other three arrow shapes

tool.arrow-left.meaning: Name of a geo shape: a block arrow pointing left. 'Left' is the direction it points, not the past tense of 'leave'.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short
Keep consistent with the other three arrow shapes

tool.arrow-right.meaning: Name of a geo shape: a block arrow pointing right. 'Right' is a direction, not 'correct' or 'entitlement'.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short
Keep consistent with the other three arrow shapes

tool.arrow-up.meaning: Name of a geo shape: a block arrow pointing upward. 'Up' is the direction it points.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short
Keep consistent with the other three arrow shapes

tool.aspect-ratio.meaning: Tooltip of the image toolbar button (and command palette submenu) that opens the list of crop proportions for the selected image. Choosing one crops the image to that ratio.
constraints: Use the locale's standard photo/image term for aspect ratio

tool.aspect-ratio.circle.meaning: Crop option for an image: crops it to a 1:1 area masked as a circle. Shown in the image toolbar's aspect-ratio menu and the command palette.
constraints: Keep '(1:1)' exactly

tool.aspect-ratio.landscape.meaning: Crop option for an image: crops it to a horizontal 4:3 rectangle. 'Landscape' is the orientation (wider than tall), not scenery.
constraints: Keep '(4:3)' exactly
Trap: use the page/photo orientation term, not the word for a natural landscape

tool.aspect-ratio.original.meaning: Crop option for an image: restores the image's original proportions (its native aspect ratio). Adjective referring to the ratio.
constraints: May need to agree with the locale's word for aspect ratio/proportion

tool.aspect-ratio.portrait.meaning: Crop option for an image: crops it to a vertical 3:4 rectangle. 'Portrait' is the orientation (taller than wide), not a picture of a person.
constraints: Keep '(3:4)' exactly
Trap: use the page/photo orientation term, not the word for a painted portrait

tool.aspect-ratio.square.meaning: Crop option for an image: crops it to a 1:1 square (rectangular corners, unlike the Circle option).
constraints: Keep '(1:1)' exactly
Square as a shape, not a town square

tool.aspect-ratio.wide.meaning: Option in the image crop 'Aspect ratio' dropdown (and command palette submenu) that crops the selected image to a wide 16:9 frame. 'Wide' describes the frame's shape (widescreen), not width as a measurement.
constraints: Keep the ratio '(16:9)' exactly as written
Should match the sibling options Original, Square (1:1), Circle (1:1), Landscape (4:3), Portrait (3:4)

tool.bookmark.meaning: Display name of the bookmark shape: a card on the canvas showing a link preview (title, description, image) for a URL. Returned as the shape's name, e.g. for accessibility labels and shape listings. A web link bookmark, not a book page marker.
constraints: Noun; shape name

tool.check-box.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool: a square with a check mark inside it. It is a drawn shape, not an interactive form control, though the usual word for a checkbox is appropriate.
constraints: Toolbar/menu tooltip; keep short
Should stay parallel with 'X box' (a square with an X)

tool.cloud.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool that draws a cloud-shaped outline (like a thought bubble). The weather/drawing shape, not cloud computing or storage.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.comment.meaning: Name of the comment tool (shortcut C). Selecting it lets the user click the canvas to place a comment thread; from the context menu it opens the comment composer where the menu was opened. Tool names are nouns: 'a comment', not the verb 'to comment'.
constraints: Toolbar/quick-action/context-menu label; keep short

tool.diamond.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool that draws a diamond (a square rotated 45°, lozenge). The geometric shape, not the gemstone or the card suit.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short
Must stay distinct from 'Rhombus'

tool.draw.meaning: Name of the freehand drawing (pen) tool: the user drags on the canvas to draw strokes. It's a tool name shown in the toolbar, so a noun such as 'pen'/'drawing' or the language's conventional tool label, not an imperative command.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.ellipse.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool that draws an ellipse/circle.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short
Must stay distinct from 'Oval', which is a separate (pill/capsule-like) geo shape

tool.embed.meaning: Name of the embed tool: opens a dialog to insert embedded web content (YouTube, Figma, Google Maps, etc.) from a URL onto the canvas. Noun for the tool ('embed', embedded content), not a command.
constraints: Toolbar/menu label; keep short

tool.eraser.meaning: Name of the eraser tool: dragging over shapes deletes them.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; noun; keep short

tool.frame.meaning: Name of the frame tool: draws a frame, a rectangular container that groups and clips the shapes inside it (like an artboard/slide). Not a picture frame or a video frame.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; noun; keep short

tool.hand.meaning: Name of the hand tool: dragging pans the canvas view. The 'hand' is the grabbing/panning cursor; many apps call it the hand or pan tool. Not a body part in a literal sense or a hand of cards.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; noun; keep short

tool.heart.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool that draws a heart shape.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.hexagon.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool that draws a six-sided polygon.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.highlight.meaning: Name of the highlighter tool: a freehand pen that draws thick, semi-transparent strokes like a highlighter marker. A tool name (the highlighter), not the verb 'to highlight' or text selection highlighting.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; noun; keep short

tool.image-crop.meaning: Button on the image toolbar (and the 'crop-image' action in menus) that enters crop mode for the selected image, showing a zoom slider, aspect ratio choices and a confirm button.
constraints: Button tooltip / menu item; use the locale's form for commands

tool.image-crop-confirm.meaning: Check-mark icon button shown while cropping an image; clicking it finishes cropping and keeps the crop. Tooltip text for the button.
constraints: Button tooltip; one word if possible
Same English as tool.media-alt-text-confirm; keep them consistent

tool.image-toolbar-title.meaning: Title/accessible label of the contextual toolbar that appears above a selected image, and the group heading for image commands in the command palette. 'Tools' here means a set of controls for the image.
constraints: Keep short

tool.image-zoom.meaning: Label and tooltip of the slider shown while cropping an image; dragging it zooms the image in or out within its crop area. It names the slider (zoom level), not a command to zoom the canvas.
constraints: Slider label; one word if possible

tool.laser.meaning: Name of the laser pointer tool: drawing with it leaves a temporary glowing trail that fades away, for pointing things out during presentations or collaboration.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; noun; keep short ('laser pointer' sense)

tool.line.meaning: Name of the line tool: draws straight line segments (with extra points for polylines). Geometric line, not a queue or a line of text.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; noun; keep short

tool.media.meaning: Name of the toolbar item that opens a file picker to insert an image or video onto the canvas. 'Media' as in images/videos.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; noun; keep short

tool.media-alt-text.meaning: Alt text for an image or video: the accessibility description read by screen readers. Tooltip of the image/video toolbar button that opens the alt-text editor, and command palette item to set it.
constraints: Use the locale's established accessibility term for alt text

tool.media-alt-text-confirm.meaning: Check-mark icon button next to the alt-text input; clicking it saves the entered alternative text for the image/video and closes the editor. Tooltip text.
constraints: Button tooltip; one word if possible
Same English as tool.image-crop-confirm; keep consistent

tool.media-alt-text-desc.meaning: Placeholder (and aria-label) of the text input where the user types the alt text describing an image or video, also used as the command palette prompt placeholder. Invites the user to write a description.
constraints: Input placeholder; keep the trailing ellipsis character …
Polite instruction addressed to the user, in the locale's UI register

tool.note.meaning: Name of the sticky note tool: places a square, coloured sticky note (Post-it style) the user can type in. Not a musical note or a footnote.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; noun; keep short

tool.octagon.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool that draws an eight-sided polygon.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.oval.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool that draws an oval: an elongated, pill/stadium-like rounded shape, separate from the Ellipse tool.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short
Must be a different word from the one used for 'Ellipse'

tool.pentagon.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool that draws a five-sided polygon. The shape, not the US defence building.
constraints: Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.pointer-down.meaning: Row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog (Tools section) describing the ',' (comma) key, which acts like pressing the mouse/pen button down at the cursor position. 'Pointer' is the mouse/pen input device or cursor; 'down' means pressed, not a downward direction.
constraints: Shortcut list label; keep short
Trap: not 'pointer pointing downward' or 'arrow down'

tool.rectangle.meaning: Name of the geo shape tool that draws a rectangle. Shown in the toolbar/shape picker tooltip, menus and keyboard shortcuts dialog.
constraints: Tool name: noun
Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.replace-media.meaning: Button in the image and video contextual toolbars (and the matching image-replace / video-replace actions) that opens a file picker so the user can swap the selected image or video for another file, keeping the shape. The ellipsis signals a further step (file picker).
constraints: Keep the trailing ellipsis (…)
'Replace' means swap for a different file, not move back to a place
'Media' covers both images and videos

tool.rhombus.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool. In tldraw the 'rhombus' geo is drawn as a slanted parallelogram leaning right; it is distinct from the separate 'Diamond' shape (a square standing on its point).
constraints: Tool name: noun
Must stay distinct from the 'Diamond' tool label
Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.rhombus-2.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool: the rhombus (slanted parallelogram) mirrored so it leans to the left. 'Left' is a direction describing the shape, not the verb 'left' (departed).
constraints: Tool name: noun phrase
Must stay distinct from 'Rhombus' and 'Diamond'
Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.rich-text-bold.meaning: Button in the floating text-formatting toolbar shown while editing text; toggles bold on the selected text. Also labels the Cmd+B row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog.
constraints: Typographic term for bold weight
Icon button tooltip; keep short

tool.rich-text-bulletList.meaning: Button in the text-formatting toolbar that toggles a bulleted (unordered) list on the current text. Also labels the Cmd+Shift+8 row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog.
constraints: Icon button tooltip; keep short
Keep distinct from 'Ordered list' and 'Task list'

tool.rich-text-code.meaning: Button in the text-formatting toolbar that toggles inline code formatting (monospace) on the selected text. Also labels the Cmd+E row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog. 'Code' means program code, not a password or postal/numeric code.
constraints: Icon button tooltip; keep short

tool.rich-text-header.meaning: Row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog's Text formatting section for Cmd+Alt+1–6, which turns the current text into a heading of level 1–6. 'Header' here means a text heading, not a page header/footer area or an HTTP header.
constraints: Use the locale's usual word for a text heading

tool.rich-text-highlight.meaning: Button in the text-formatting toolbar that toggles a highlighter-style background mark on the selected text. Also labels the Cmd+Shift+H row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog. Not the 'Highlight' drawing tool (tool.highlight), though the sense is the same marker-pen highlighting.
constraints: Icon button tooltip; keep short
Means marker highlighting, not 'emphasise/feature'

tool.rich-text-italic.meaning: Button in the text-formatting toolbar that toggles italic on the selected text. Also labels the Cmd+I row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog.
constraints: Typographic term
Icon button tooltip; keep short

tool.rich-text-link.meaning: Button in the text-formatting toolbar that opens the link editor to add or edit a hyperlink on the selected text. Also labels the Cmd+Shift+K row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog. 'Link' is a web hyperlink.
constraints: Icon button tooltip; keep short

tool.rich-text-link-remove.meaning: Icon button in the link editor (inside the text-formatting toolbar) that removes the hyperlink from the selected text, leaving the text itself.
constraints: Removes only the link, does not delete text
Icon button tooltip; keep short

tool.rich-text-link-visit.meaning: Icon button in the link editor that opens the link's URL in a new browser tab.
constraints: Means open/go to the URL
Icon button tooltip; keep short

tool.rich-text-orderedList.meaning: Row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog's Text formatting section for Cmd+Shift+7, which toggles a numbered list. 'Ordered' means numbered, not 'tidy' or 'commanded'.
constraints: Use the locale's usual term for a numbered list
Keep distinct from 'Bulleted list'

tool.rich-text-strikethrough.meaning: Row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog's Text formatting section for Cmd+Shift+S, which toggles strikethrough (a line through the text) on the selection.
constraints: Typographic term

tool.rich-text-taskItem-toggle.meaning: Row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog's Text formatting section for Cmd+Enter, which checks or unchecks the checkbox of the current item in a task (checklist) list. 'Tick' means mark as done with a check mark, not a clock tick or an insect.
constraints: Action toggles the checkbox (check/uncheck)
Keep 'task item' consistent with 'Task list'

tool.rich-text-taskList.meaning: Button in the text-formatting toolbar that toggles a task list (checklist with tickable checkboxes) on the current text. Also labels the Cmd+Shift+9 row in the keyboard shortcuts dialog.
constraints: Icon button tooltip; keep short
Means a checklist, not a to-do app or job queue

tool.rich-text-toolbar-title.meaning: Accessible label (for screen readers) of the floating toolbar that appears above text while editing it, holding bold, italic, link, list and highlight buttons.
constraints: Accessibility-only label for the toolbar; not visible text

tool.select.meaning: Name of the selection tool (the arrow pointer) in the main toolbar, used to select, move and resize shapes. A tool name rather than a one-off command.
constraints: Tool name; use the form the locale uses for the select/pointer tool
Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.star.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool that draws a five-pointed star shape.
constraints: Tool name: noun (the shape, not a favourite/rating)
Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.text.meaning: Name of the text tool in the main toolbar, which creates a text shape on the canvas.
constraints: Tool name: noun
Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.trapezoid.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool that draws a trapezoid (four sides, one pair parallel, wider at the bottom).
constraints: Tool name: noun
Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.triangle.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool that draws a triangle.
constraints: Tool name: noun
Toolbar tooltip; keep short

tool.video-toolbar-title.meaning: Accessible label (for screen readers) of the contextual toolbar shown when a video shape is selected (e.g. replace media, alt text).
constraints: Accessibility-only label for the toolbar; not visible text

tool.x-box.meaning: Name of a geo shape tool that draws a rectangle with an X (two diagonals) through it. 'X' is the letter-shaped cross mark, not the Xbox brand.
constraints: Tool name: noun
Pairs with 'Check box' (box with a check mark)
Toolbar tooltip; keep short

ui.checked.meaning: Accessible label on the check-mark icon of a checkbox menu item or checkable button, announced when the option is on/selected.
constraints: Screen-reader state, not visible
Means 'ticked/on', not 'verified/inspected'
Pairs with 'Unchecked'

ui.close.meaning: Accessible label of the X icon button in the top corner of every dialog; closes the dialog.
constraints: Verb (close the dialog), not the adjective 'near'
aria-label for an icon button

ui.unchecked.meaning: Accessible label on the checkbox icon of a checkbox menu item or checkable button, announced when the option is off/not selected.
constraints: Screen-reader state, not visible
Means 'not ticked/off', not 'unverified'
Pairs with 'Checked'

verticalAlign-style.end.meaning: Option in the style panel's vertical-align picker (and command palette) that places a shape's label text at the bottom of the shape.
constraints: Position word, not 'end/finish'
Option tooltip in an icon picker; keep short
Siblings: 'Top', 'Middle'

verticalAlign-style.middle.meaning: Option in the style panel's vertical-align picker (and command palette) that vertically centres a shape's label text within the shape.
constraints: Vertical position (centred), not horizontal
Option tooltip in an icon picker; keep short
Siblings: 'Top', 'Bottom'

verticalAlign-style.start.meaning: Option in the vertical alignment style picker (style panel and command palette) that places a shape's label at the top of the shape. 'Top' is a position, not 'best' or a garment/toy.
constraints: Pairs with 'Middle' and 'Bottom'; keep short, matching their form

vscode.file-open.backup.meaning: Button on a VS Code notification shown when an old (v1) .tldr file is opened and upgraded. Clicking it copies the original file next to it as '<name> - old.tldr'. Imperative 'make a backup', not the noun.
constraints: VS Code notification button; keep short

vscode.file-open.backup-failed.meaning: VS Code notification shown when the user asked to back up an upgraded old file but the file doesn't have the .tldr extension, so no backup was made.
constraints: Keep '.tldr' unchanged

vscode.file-open.backup-saved.meaning: Confirmation in a VS Code notification that the backup copy of the original old file was written. The code appends ': <filename>' after it.
constraints: Followed by a colon and the backup file name, so it must read naturally before ': filename'

vscode.file-open.desc.meaning: Text of the VS Code notification shown when an old-format .tldr file is opened: the document was upgraded to the current tldraw format, and the user can make a backup of the original, which still opens on old.tldraw.com.
constraints: 'click below' refers to the notification's Backup button; keep old.tldraw.com unchanged

vscode.file-open.dont-show-again.meaning: Button on the old-file upgrade notification in VS Code. Clicking it stops this notification from appearing in future.
constraints: Notification button; keep short

vscode.file-open.open.meaning: Button on the old-file upgrade notification in VS Code that dismisses it and keeps working with the upgraded document, without making a backup.
constraints: Notification button; keep short
